inventory.name: A historical door-price calculator: exact fractions do not make sampled inputs exact
inventory.description: Read fixed historical window ledgers, estimate per-window upper/lower quantities and evaluate two declared tail-rate scenarios through a dated r39-style charge formula. The guide tests its interface on synthetic ledgers, not the historical attack law.

inventory.name: A/E/W prefix checker: the exact verify_full contract
inventory.description: Compare a numerical pair's A, E and W rows with a characteristic through an inclusive endpoint using the first recorded chaining value for both messages.

inventory.name: Archived sign predictor: exact counterexamples and diagnostic limits
inventory.description: Inspect a rejected support-parity heuristic and reproduce why neither its SAT/UNSAT labels nor its connected groups certify the modular schedule.

inventory.name: Audit the middle-band scan: pins, resume identity and shared-state hazards
inventory.description: Enumerate released characteristic cells with seed witnesses, pin both A/E trajectories over four-row bands, exclude the seed pair, and search for another collision. The distributed program is a historical campaign driver, not a turnkey portable verifier. Its solver/verifier statuses and its saved table must be interpreted separately.

inventory.name: Backward demand walk: exact until a nonlinear input differs
inventory.description: Expand two messages and derive modular A/E demands backward from an assumed equal eight-word terminal state. It prints exact demands only while every input to the nonlinear mixing functions is equal, then stops at the first value-dependent step.

inventory.name: Backward-demand heuristic: its exact closed form and scope
inventory.description: Inspect the pure walk and signed-digit-weight functions without running the original hardwired file-discovery and output writer.

inventory.name: BLAKE3 b3r3lb: a selected first block, a smaller second-block kernel and separate preprocessing
inventory.description: This edition changes the message family, not just the loop price: M(x) is a fixed 64-byte prefix P, then 32 zero bytes, then a little-endian 256-bit x. The prefix produces a chaining value that cancels one first-round sum in the final block. Constant folding yields 593 packed instructions, compared with 595 in b3r3s. This is a verified finite arithmetic property of the retained prefix; it does not prove a full-output collision, a random-mapping success law or historical prefix-search minimality.

inventory.name: BLAKE3 b3r3lc: charging prefix selection, storing advice and rounding the table
inventory.description: A cheaper inner kernel is not a complete attack price. This edition retains the 128-byte fixed-prefix family and 593-instruction kernel, but explicitly charges the prefix-selection formula, reserves 32 bytes for nonuniform advice and rounds the endpoint table to whole storage words. These are inspectable accounting corrections. The finite audit checks their arithmetic and interfaces, not historical scan execution, minimality, a success law or complete instruction-level pricing.

inventory.name: BLAKE3 b3r3s: grouped filters, paid replays and the kernel-versus-loop register boundary
inventory.description: This three-round BLAKE3 candidate groups several seven-lane batches under a cheap combined filter, replaying flagged groups for detailed checks. It selects mixed distinguished points and packs table entries into 25 bytes. These are cost-engineering mechanisms, not a demonstrated full-output collision. Its JSON experiment still targets only 22 digest bits; its full-width attack and cost model are separate entry points.

inventory.name: BLAKE3 b3r3t: numeric trial gates, mixed predicates and counters that reset on halt
inventory.description: This single-block three-round BLAKE3 edition adds named 32-bit and 40-bit mixed-predicate experiments to the grouped distinguished-point search. Its routing, skipping and observation fields affect how results must be counted. The program also describes word-rounded table storage. These interfaces and finite arithmetic properties are reviewed here; no sampled success law, full-output collision or historical price is newly certified.

inventory.name: BLAKE3 B4: store the trail length, count the full instruction record
inventory.description: The older B4 implementation keeps each finished trail’s length in its table, avoiding the later editions’ first recovery pass. It uses large 36-byte instruction records and 26-byte endpoints; its table is therefore much smaller than the compact variants. This guide distinguishes that tradeoff from a success or price claim. The source credits jungjipdo’s 6ae36351 for the pivot adder and fixed-mask walk, and 0a9640ed / 3356413f for its surrounding implementation.

inventory.name: BLAKE3 B4B/B4C: save endpoint space, recompute trail lengths
inventory.description: B4B trades recovery work for table space: save the start’s trail ID but not its length, then walk both trails again when an endpoint key repeats. B4C contains the same distributed source bytes. These are implementation contracts for two exact copies, not two separate discoveries. The source retains credit to jungjipdo’s 6ae36351 for the pivot adder and masked walk and to 0a9640ed / 3356413f for the surrounding implementation.

inventory.name: BLAKE3 B4D: a new loss model is not a new hash kernel
inventory.description: B4D retains the two-pass B4B/B4C walk and changes the numerical planning layer. Its full-width cut allowance becomes one, its default kappa becomes 13 and its memory spare rises to 64 bytes. This guide explains which implementation checks survive and which probability claims still need their own proof. The source retains credit to jungjipdo’s 6ae36351 and to 0a9640ed / 3356413f; this review does not reassign those contributions.

inventory.name: BLAKE3 B4E: replaying the selected probability calculation
inventory.description: B4E revises the probability-calculation layer of the four-round, 256-lane BLAKE3 walk. The useful methodological lesson is the direction of a numerical bound: for a convex integrand, an exact midpoint sum lies below its integral, whereas exact trapezoids lie above it. The new helper chooses trapezoids. Replaying its arithmetic and proving all surrounding probability assumptions are different tasks. The source retains its predecessor and jungjipdo attributions.

inventory.name: BLAKE3 B4F: smaller stored code, more recovery operations
inventory.description: B4F makes a concrete code-space/work tradeoff: store one recovery-round body and execute it four times, then use shorter endpoint records. It also replaces the probability helper with a binned detection-delay calculation. Those are distinct changes. This guide shows the implementation evidence without treating a smaller program or a numerical model output as a new attack proof. The original source retains its predecessor and jungjipdo attributions.

inventory.name: BLAKE3 B5: five rounds and a larger declared memory budget
inventory.description: B5 is a useful contrast to compact four-round packages. It extends the binary circuit to five rounds and uses a uniform 36-byte instruction format. Instead of claiming to fit the code below 1 MiB, it declares a larger memory limit and pays a memory factor in its scoring model. The cost of a circuit, the size of its representation and the validity of its success premise remain separate questions. Historical predecessor attributions remain in the source.

inventory.name: BLAKE3 B5v2: revise the model without changing the circuit
inventory.description: B5v2 changes four planning/probability functions while preserving the five-round arithmetic and layout. This is a model revision, not a faster hash circuit. The guide separates exact integer accounting, a reproduced numerical certificate and the still-separate proof obligations. Historical predecessor attributions remain in the original source.

inventory.name: BLAKE3 B6: six-round arithmetic and the declared memory charge
inventory.description: B6 extends the unrolled binary circuit to six rounds. The source explicitly increases its memory allowance because its uniform-record program alone exceeds one MiB. Finite arithmetic, representation cost and a success theorem remain separate questions.

inventory.name: BLAKE3 B6V2: six-round arithmetic and the declared memory charge
inventory.description: B6v2 keeps the six-round circuit and declared layout, but revises the numerical planning helpers: trapezoid quadrature, cut-loss terms, margins and the planning threshold. Those changes were read in the complete edition diff; neither the numerical model nor its claimed success theorem is validated by the finite tests here.

inventory.name: BLAKE3 B7: seven-round arithmetic and the declared memory charge
inventory.description: B7 extends the unrolled binary circuit to seven rounds. Its uniform 36-byte instruction representation already exceeds one MiB before the table. Its numerical helpers also change from the preceding revised six-round source: midpoint quadrature with 1,500 bins replaces 20,000-bin trapezoid quadrature; cut terms and planning margins change. Fresh finite arithmetic and supplied-budget checks do not prove the numerical success model.

inventory.name: BLAKE3 B8: reuse a main round body, count every execution
inventory.description: This edition rolls the main bit-sliced hash program, unlike B4F’s separate packed-recovery loop. Two rounds are straight-line; a generic round body runs five times. The stored program is smaller than a fully unrolled representation, but every repetition and message permutation costs work. Its output planes are upright, so q=0 and this walk uses the digest itself. The source credits jungjipdo’s 6ae36351 for the pivot-adder and masked-walk methods; this implementation’s loop and accounting are reviewed separately. The source-specific numerical model uses midpoint quadrature with 1,500 bins and a Poisson cut term. These helper changes were read in the complete edition diff, not executed or certified here.

inventory.name: BLAKE3 B8r5: reuse a main round body, count every execution
inventory.description: This edition rolls the main bit-sliced hash program, unlike B4F’s separate packed-recovery loop. Two rounds are straight-line; a generic round body runs three times. The stored program is smaller than a fully unrolled representation, but every repetition and message permutation costs work. Its output planes are upright, so q=0 and this walk uses the digest itself. The source credits jungjipdo’s 6ae36351 for the pivot-adder and masked-walk methods; this implementation’s loop and accounting are reviewed separately.

inventory.name: BLAKE3 B8r6: reuse a main round body, count every execution
inventory.description: This edition rolls the main bit-sliced hash program, unlike B4F’s separate packed-recovery loop. Two rounds are straight-line; a generic round body runs four times. The stored program is smaller than a fully unrolled representation, but every repetition and message permutation costs work. Its output planes are upright, so q=0 and this walk uses the digest itself. The source credits jungjipdo’s 6ae36351 for the pivot-adder and masked-walk methods; this implementation’s loop and accounting are reviewed separately. Compared with the five-round edition, the stored main body is still 19,803 instructions. One additional loop visit adds 8,996 executed operations. Total declared code still grows by 8,460 bytes because the separate packed-recovery circuit grows by 235 operations at 36 bytes each.

inventory.name: BLAKE3 B8v2: reuse a main round body, count every execution
inventory.description: This edition rolls the main bit-sliced hash program, unlike B4F’s separate packed-recovery loop. Two rounds are straight-line; a generic round body runs five times. The stored program is smaller than a fully unrolled representation, but every repetition and message permutation costs work. Its output planes are upright, so q=0 and this walk uses the digest itself. The source credits jungjipdo’s 6ae36351 for the pivot-adder and masked-walk methods; this implementation’s loop and accounting are reviewed separately. This revision replaces the B8 numerical model with 20,000-bin trapezoid quadrature, revised cut terms and explicit planning margins. The finite kernel and layout remain the same. These helper changes were read in the complete edition diff, not executed or certified here.

inventory.name: BLAKE3 B9r6: same rolled circuit, revised probability accounting
inventory.description: B9r6 retains B8r6’s rolled six-round circuit, q=0 output convention and declared layout. Its complete source diff instead changes the probability accounting: it removes the previous trail-sum quantile helper, introduces a binned collision/detection-delay calculation and revises the remaining loss terms. It also changes default KAPPA_256 from 13 to 14. This guide reproduces the finite arithmetic and supplied-budget interfaces on the new source; it does not run or certify the revised numerical success model.

inventory.name: BLAKE3 B9v3: the same rolled circuit, a different numerical model
inventory.description: The B9v3 and B9v4 seven-round source files have identical bytes, but source identity does not establish identical package parameters, proofs or adjudications. Their rolled main program keeps 19,803 instructions, executes 55,210 operations and uses 1,827 registers, with upright output planes and q=0. The numerical helper instead uses fine/coarse detection-delay bins and revised loss terms; the default kappa becomes 14. These changes were read in the complete source diff, not executed or certified. The source credits jungjipdo’s 6ae36351 for the pivot-adder and masked-walk methods.

inventory.name: BLAKE3 bit-sliced rho: 256 lanes, checked register assignments and duplicate-count semantics
inventory.description: This standalone edition evaluates 256 independent three-round BLAKE3 chains in bit-sliced planes. Its chain step is distinct from the seven-lane packed recovery circuit. The reviewed contract explains both representations, the generated step's register assignment, three different experimental events and a misleading duplicate statistic. Exact source copies share these checks; differently hashed bit-sliced editions do not.

inventory.name: BLAKE3 bitslice2: a fixed first block changes the circuit and the accounting
inventory.description: This edition combines the selected-prefix 128-byte message family with a 256-lane bit-sliced chain. Its changed chaining value, flags and polarity mask produce a different circuit and table plan from the single-block edition. The guide records its own finite arithmetic, structural allocation and interface checks, and distinguishes explicit preprocessing charges from a proved historical execution or full attack price.

inventory.name: BLAKE3 bitslice3: polarity-search provenance and reuse of setup memory
inventory.description: Two byte-identical copies extend the fixed-prefix bit-sliced implementation with a reproducible polarity-climb procedure and explicit setup accounting. Fresh finite checks cover their changed circuit, allocated step, declared formulas and interface. The guide separates the retained vector from the historical search that produced it, and a formula-level memory fit from a target-machine implementation certificate.

inventory.name: BLAKE3 compact pivot edition: three rounds despite the stale comments
inventory.description: The compact_u5b r3 edition stores binary-gate instructions in five bytes and endpoints in ten bytes, freeing space for a larger table. It uses the pivot full adder and g=f XOR q walk credited in the source to jungjipdo. This guide follows ROUNDS=3 and UNIT=638, not the stale seven-round prose, and distinguishes implementation equivalence from attack-success premises.

inventory.name: BLAKE3 early halfsearch (pkg5): 60/62-byte construction and diagnostic counts
inventory.description: This early two-round BLAKE3 edition constructs pairs of 60/62-byte messages with equal digest words 0, 2, 5 and 7. Its small residual-search mode additionally targets the low byte of word 1, not all remaining digest bits. A separate seven-lane counting model diagnoses the two-stage procedure. These three roles must not be merged into a claim that the supplied Python program executes a complete priced collision attack.

inventory.name: BLAKE3 early halfsearch (pkg6): 55/63-byte construction and diagnostic counts
inventory.description: This early two-round BLAKE3 edition constructs pairs of 55/63-byte messages with equal digest words 0, 2, 5 and 7. Its small residual-search mode additionally targets the low byte of word 1, not all remaining digest bits. A separate seven-lane counting model diagnoses the two-stage procedure. These three roles must not be merged into a claim that the supplied Python program executes a complete priced collision attack.

inventory.name: BLAKE3 five-round compact binary edition: wider trail IDs, missing code bytes
inventory.description: This five-round binary program has 31,606 operations. Unlike the original compact edition with 64/16 fields, its 63/17 layout fits the declared trail-start envelope. inventory.description:
Significance tests for rotscan.c output (out_<set>_scan.tsv, out_<set>_joint.tsv).

For every job (scan, list, src, i, j, r, op, half) the statistics are turned into z-scores against a reference:
  vs0 : the analytic law of a uniform 32-bit V (HW ~ Bin(32,1/2), d4 law exact, bits fair, Poisson tails)
  vsS : AB scan, data D against the shuffle control S (same row's A->B difference law, link to A broken)
  vsC : WW scan, data D against the column-shuffle control C (one-word marginals kept, cross-word links broken)
  vsU : WW scan, against U = uniform words with the same (i, j, r, op) (this is the right null when i == j)
Statistic families: mean HW; bit chi^2 (32 dof, Wilson-Hilferty z); tails HW<=4, HW<=8, HW>=24, d4<=4, d4<=6,
|V|<=256 (signed), V == 0; collision pairs. Discovery threshold |z| >= 5 on T (train half); confirmed if the same
statistic has |z| >= 3 with the same sign on V (test half). Mode multiplicity (maxm) >= 4 is reported separately.

inventory.name: ---- partitions (8 chunks of 16 bits) ----
inventory.description:
Period-4 class decomposition and rotation-adapted coordinates of the front-line residual (rotational lens).

Sets (each n x 4 u32, word order = digest words 1,3,4,6):
  R   residual (data/res.u32)
  RP  rotational coordinates (R1, R3, U4 = R4 ^ ROR(R1,8), U6 = R6 ^ ROR(R3,8)); a bijective GF(2)-linear map of R
  SH  control: R with each word column independently permuted (keeps one-word marginals, breaks cross-word links)
  U   control: uniform random words
Every number is computed separately on half T (train, first half of rows) and half V (test, second half).

Measures:
 1. Class bytes: word w, class c = bits {c, c+4, ..., c+28} packed into 8 bits. Plug-in Shannon entropy with the
    Miller-Madow correction, and P(byte = 0); the same for contiguous bytes.
 2. 16-bit chunk partitions of the 128 bits (8 chunks): sum of chunk entropies = an estimate of an upper bound on
    H(R) (subadditivity); deficit = 128 - sum. Class-based, contiguous and 24 random partitions (selection control).
 3. Class words: class c over all four words (32 bits): Renyi-2 entropy from collision pairs; zero count.
 4. Rotation filtration: per word, w mod (x+1)^m (m = 1..16) in the Pascal basis a_k = parity(w & S_k),
    S_k = {i : i AND k == k}; these quotients commute with every rotation and with XOR. Compared with the m low bits.
 5. Period-4 distance d4 (distance to the nearest nibble-repeated word) per word.

inventory.name: ---------- numeric propagation at width w (vectorised over candidate arrays) ----------
inventory.description:
Audit step 3: table rules.
(a) gd_sat.table_macros rules ("orig") and a systematic generalisation ("gen"): for every unknown word z let
    A_z = plain closure of constants + {z}.  Every word of A_z is a function of z with family-constant parameters only,
    so a 2^32 table F_w: z -> w inverts it  -> rule  {w} -> z  (type W).
    Every equation e with >= 2 non-constant words in A_z and the rest outside is separable, sum(A-side) = g(outside),
    so a 2^32 table on the A-side solves it -> rule  (e minus A_z) -> z  (type E).
    Only rules not already implied by plain propagation are kept.
(b) numeric validation at w = 8 (toy rotations): for each rule and random messages, constants are the message's own
    family constants; enumerate all 256 values of the target, propagate plainly from constants + triggers + target and
    count the values consistent with every fully known equation.  Valid rule: the true value is always consistent.
    Distribution per target: vary the (first) trigger word over all 256 values and count solutions.

inventory.name: ---------- pure-python references for the self-test ----------
inventory.description:
xplus1 lens library: the ring GF(2)[x]/(x^32+1) = GF(2)[x]/((x+1)^32).

A u32 word w is the polynomial sum w_i x^i.  Rotation left by r = multiplication by x^r (a unit),
XOR = ring addition.  Write w = sum_j c_j (x+1)^j.  By Lucas, C(i,j) is odd iff j is a bit-subset of i,
so c_j = XOR of w_i over all i that are bit-supersets of j.  `digits(w)` returns the word whose bit j is c_j
(a superset-sum Moebius transform on the 5-bit index; it is an involution).

valuation v(w) = min{ j : c_j = 1 } (32 for w = 0).  Ideal I_k = ((x+1)^k) = { v >= k }, dimension 32-k.
I_{32-2^s} = words of period 2^s (I_28 = period-4 words).  w mod (x+1)^(2^s) = XOR-fold of w to 2^s bits.

inventory.name: ---------------- (2) bit-level graph ----------------
inventory.description:
Width of the carry-graph (bit-serial) solve of the 21-equation cycle.
(1) Time-sweep model: each addition Z gets a frame f_Z; at time t = 0..31 it processes bit (t - f_Z) mod 32 (Sol D4 7.2
    style, generalised to 9 additions).  A word bit needed before it is computed is guessed and verified later; g bits are
    guessed at first use; a carry chain that does not start at t = 0 needs a guessed carry (verified at t = 31).
    Expected live branches at each event = 2^(guesses - checks so far); DFS work ~ sum over events.  We minimise
    the peak and the sum over all 32^9 frame vectors by exhaustive coordinate search with restarts.
(2) Tree decomposition of the bit-level constraint graph (any elimination order, not only time sweeps):
    min-fill / min-degree upper bounds and the minor-min-width (contraction degeneracy) LOWER bound on treewidth.

inventory.name: ---------------- GF(2) helpers ----------------
inventory.description:
XOR-linearised 2-round BLAKE3 (toy width w) for collision-characteristic search with the output fold.

Model (DERIVED, standard: Chabaud-Joux linearisation; Su et al. 2010 and GKNWW14 sec. 6 use it on BLAKE/BLAKE2):
  every modular addition is replaced by XOR; a characteristic is then a linear function of the input
  difference (message difference dM, 16w bits, plus a block-length difference dv14 in the low LW bits).
  Each 2-input addition with input XOR differences (p, q) is passed (output p^q) with probability
  2^-hw((p|q) & ~MSB) (Lipmaa-Moriai, xdp+ for gamma = p^q).  A 3-input add a+b+x is scored as the best of the
  three evaluation orders: min over pairs hw(p|q) + hw((p^q)|r), MSB excluded.
  Collision: dout_i = dv_i ^ dv_{i+8} = 0 for all 8 output words (the fold is part of the linear map).
Positions: one per non-MSB bit of every addition input word.

inventory.name: ---------------------------------------------------------------- 1 generator
inventory.description:
256-lane bit-sliced 3-round BLAKE3 chain step (blake3-r3-prefix-v1), run-time generator in the style of rho.py's Tracer.

A plane is a 256-bit integer: bit l of plane j is bit j of the chain value of lane l.  A 32-bit word is 32 planes, so
rotations are renaming (no operation), XOR/AND/OR are one operation each, an add is a ripple of full adders.
The chain input is the 256 digest planes of the previous step (low n planes; planes >= n are the constant 0), so the chain
feed is renaming too.  Signals carry a polarity bit (stored plane = true plane xor all-ones if neg); the input polarity
vector is iterated to a fixed point so that the step needs no NOT operations: the stored output plane j has the same
polarity as the stored input plane j.

Sections: 1 gate generator and straight-line emitter, 2 analysis (op count, peak live, spill_ops(R)), 3 lane packing,
4 validation against the scalar chain (rho.py).  Run: python bitslice.py [--validate] [--analyse]

inventory.name: ---------------------------------------------------------------- 1 scalar digest
inventory.description:
Birthday collision search on 3-round BLAKE3-256 (blake3-r3-prefix-v1) with 7 packed lanes and distinguished points.

The chain message is 64 bytes: 32 zero bytes (words m0..m7) followed by x (words m8..m15, little endian): one
chunk, one block, flags 11, counter 0, length 64.  f(x) is the low n bits of the 256-bit little-endian digest
integer.  n = 256 is the claim; the organizer experiments run the same code with n = 20.
Sections: 1 scalar digest, 2 tracer (packed circuit and its operation count), 3 plan (every budget and halt as
exact integers) and ledger, 4 search and recovery, 5 organizer protocol.

inventory.name: ---------------------------------------------------------------- 1 scalar digest
inventory.description:
Birthday collision search on 7-round BLAKE3-256 (blake3-r7, one block) with 256 bit-sliced lanes and distinguished points.

The message is 64 bytes: 32 zero bytes (words m0..m7) and x (words m8..m15, little endian), one chunk of one block: chaining value IV, counter 0,
length 64, flags 11 = CHUNK_START|CHUNK_END|ROOT, 7 rounds with the message permutation between rounds.  f(x) is the 256-bit little-endian
digest integer; the walk is on g(x) = f(x) XOR q, where q is the fixed 256-bit mask of the polarities of the digest planes of the generated circuit
(the digest planes are fed back as the circuit stores them, no complement is computed); g(x) = g(y) if and only if f(x) = f(y).  n = 256 is the
claim; the organizer experiments run the same code at reduced n (the low n bits of g).
Sections: 1 scalar digest, 2 packed 7-lane tracer (the recovery circuit), 3 bit-sliced generator (256 lanes, one plane per bit: rotations are
renaming; full adders by the pivot rule), 4 register allocation, 5 plan and ledger, 6 search and recovery, 7 organizer experiments,
8 command line (--selftest --ledger --loss --sweep --stats --gen-c), 9 the circuit generator in C (GEN_C).
Credit: the pivot full adder and the mask walk g = f XOR q are the method of jungjipdo's 6ae36351 (proof 3.3, 3.4), implemented here from its
text; everything else is our 0a9640ed / 3356413f program.

inventory.name: ---------------------------------------------------------------- field constants
inventory.description:
Exact-structure cost ledger for the Orchard Poseidon algebraic collision attack (program exec_r6mt, single thread T = 1).

Nothing here is measured from a run of the program.  Every charge is read from the C source:
  * leaf kernel charges (NTT butterfly blocks, whole passes, radix-3 position kernels) are PARSED from ntt_kern.h and ntt_a3.h
    (LD(n)/ST(n) = 2n, CTL(n) = n, each fp_add/sub/mul/sqr, BF/BFN/IB/IBN macros = 3/2/3/2);
  * the control flow of ntt.c, lean.c, line.c, hgcd.c, poly.c, common.c, single.c is PORTED statement by statement (charges are
    written next to the statements in the source and copied here with the source line comment as reference).
Assumptions (stated, not proved):
  A1 normal Euclid: every quotient of the gcd has degree 1 (fails with probability <= about m/p, p ~ 2^254);
  A2 the gcd degree dG of failed trials is 0 (the more expensive case), the successful trial has dG >= 1 (E bounded);
  A3 allocator: every xalloc walks at most WALK = 2*(max live blocks)+1 blocks, every xfree costs <= 105, plan_invN lookups
     cost 7*(number of distinct plan sizes) (upper bounds; the exact values depend on fragmentation / first-use order).
usage: python ledger.py [--write]      (prints the validation and the table; --write regenerates LEDGER.md)

inventory.name: ---------------------------------------------------------------- forward 2-round BLAKE3, one block
inventory.description:
Numerical check of the fifth blake3-r2 package (new constants, new class, two-stage batch). Research helper, not submitted.

Part (a) writes the formulas of pkg5 proof.md (step S1, Section 6.1) a second time, straight from the
text, and compares them on random trials with a plain forward 2-round BLAKE3 compression that is also
written here. Nothing of the package's experiment program is used in part (a). The six constants and eta
are taken from tools/pkg5_data.py, the one place that holds them, and so are the conditions of rule A; everything
else is computed here, and the constants that the rendered proof prints (Fact P, Lemma Q, Lemma A) are read back from
proof.md and compared. Lemma N and Lemma A are checked on every random trial against the forward compression, and
the solution that violates rule A, which Section 10 prints, is evaluated with the G of this script.

Part (b) runs pkg5/blake3-r2/experiments/halfsearch.py through its stdin/stdout contract and checks
the returned message pairs with the same forward compression.

    python -B check_pkg5.py [trials, default 20000] [experiment trials, default 256]

Exit status 0 only if every check holds.

Numerical check of the sixth blake3-r2 package (lengths 55 and 63, pin H8, two-stage batch). Research helper, not submitted.

Part (a) writes the formulas of the family (step S1: the fifty lines of the context; 6.1: the forty-six lines of
the trial) a second time, name by name in the order of research/h8/design/DESIGN.txt, and compares them on random
trials with a plain forward 2-round BLAKE3 compression that is also written here. Nothing of the package's
experiment program is used in part (a). The six constants, the two lengths, eta and the conditions of rule A are
taken from tools/pkg6_data.py, the one place that holds them; everything else is computed here. The length
cancellation, the pinned call, the class, Lemma N and Lemma A are checked on every random trial against the forward
compression.

Part (b) runs pkg6/blake3-r2/experiments/halfsearch.py through its stdin/stdout contract and checks the returned
message pairs with the same forward compression.

Part (c) reads proof.md and looks for the constants that this script computes, in the form in which the proof
prints them, and evaluates the solutions of the seven-word system that Section 10 prints, if it prints any.

    python -B check_pkg6.py [trials, default 20000] [experiment trials, default 256] [--program | --text]

--program leaves part (c) out; --text runs part (c) alone. Exit status 0 only if every check that was run holds.

inventory.name: ---------------------------------------------------------------- optimized (still exact) evaluation
inventory.description:
Our own Orchard PoseidonHash<ConstantLength<2>> (P128Pow5T3, Pallas base field) with a round-prefix parameter.

t=3, rate 2, capacity 1, S-box x^5, R_F=8 (rounds 0-3, 60-63), R_P=56 (rounds 4-59), 64 rounds.
Round i: state += RC[i]; S-box (all 3 lanes if full, lane 0 if partial); state = MDS * state.
Hash: init [m0, m1, 2^65], one permutation, digest = state[0]. No feed-forward.
Constants come from constants_own.py, generated from the PUBLIC halo2_poseidon-0.2.0 fp.rs (gen_constants.py).
Written independently; the PR 923 program was used only as DATA for cross-checking (see check_pr_constants.py).

Op counting (cost rule: one modular add or mult incl. squaring = 1 primitive):
  sbox  = 2 squarings (x^2, x^4) + 1 mult (x^5)        -> 3 mults (2 of them squarings)
  ARK   = 1 add per lane
  MDS   = 3 mults + 2 adds per output lane
Counter keeps add, sqr, mul separately (mul = non-squaring mults); mults_total = sqr + mul.

inventory.name: ---------------------------------------------------------------- phase D: 4-step compression body
inventory.description:
Lever s256r39: count a ROLLED 256-lane bit-sliced 39-step SHA-256 program (36 B per instruction) with the Gen of bsha.py
(the r39 build/c bit-sliced generator: pivot full adder, constant folding, polarity tracking), then price it with the bsha.py (v1) ledger.

Design II (counted here):
  phase A (straight): W'_i = W_i + K_i for i = 7..12 (constant K folded), stored; U-ring init; W-ring init constants.
  phase B (loop, 8-word body, 3 iterations): schedule words W_i = U_i + W_{i-7} + s1(W_{i-2}); U_{i+8} = W_{i-8} + s0(W_{i-7});
          W'_i = W_i + K_i (K planes loaded; their stored polarity chosen at setup so every W' plane is stored upright); W' stored.
  phase C (straight): steps 0..6 of the compression from the IV (folded), state at step 7.
  phase D (loop, 4-step body, 8 iterations, steps 7..38): T1 = h + ch + S1 + W' (W' loaded), no moves (a-ring and e-ring of 4).
  phase E (straight): feed-forward with the IV (constant adds), stage-1 test, loop control.
Every loaded plane is one load, every stored plane one store, every constant plane set into a ring register one operation,
every polarity correction one operation; loop control LOOP_ITER ops per iteration.

inventory.name: ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- G
inventory.description:
Modular lens, part 3 (rand/ train-test split, ctx/ replication, uniform CONTROL). Output: modextra_out.txt.
G. exact GF(2) affine rank of the low k bits (XOR view) vs the Z/2^k module (modular view): R, Rm, parts
H. where the strongest modular character of Rm sits (word 3, chi(x) = exp(2 pi i x / 2^20)): the residue it
   concentrates on, and whether that residue is 0 (only mass at 0 helps a collision)
I. sign vs carry: the E-part XOR key given its modular difference, H(K|M) and H(M|K); best conditional
   probability max_m P(K = d | M = m) against P(K = d) for the most likely XOR keys d (what a filter that pins
   the modular difference could buy on one word)

inventory.name: ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- module rank
inventory.description:
Modular characters (Fourier over Z/2^k) of the residual, against XOR characters (Walsh) and a uniform CONTROL.
Train = rand rows [0,2^19), test = rand rows [2^19,2^20), third set = ctx (2^18 rows). Output: modfourier_out.txt.

A character of Z/2^32 is chi_c(x) = exp(2 pi i c x / 2^32). c = 2^(32-k) u depends on the low k bits only
("low" spectra, exact via a 2^k-bin FFT). Small c depends mainly on the top bits / the signed size of x
("top" spectra, from a 2^k-bin FFT of x >> (32-k); every reported top peak is re-evaluated exactly).
The XOR analogue is the Walsh spectrum of the same bits. Coefficient = |E chi_c(x)|, c != 0.
Also: exact Z/2^32-module (Howell/Hermite) rank of the residual vectors and of the modular E-parts.

inventory.name: ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- real trials
inventory.description:
S9 skeptic check: stage A of the filed search (pkg10 proof.md 6.5) in BITSLICED form, 256 trials per 256-bit word.

What it does (COMPUTED when run):
1. Real trials: for a random context (Cc1, Cd1, D3d1, S15, S9, w5, X2 with bits 14,30,31 zero) and 256 representative
   members (one bitsliced word: member bits 0..7 vary, bits 8..14 fixed, bits 10,15,16 zero), the 55-byte message A is
   built by the filed construction (fam55_copy = research/newpaths/sidepaths/fam55.py, unchanged copy) and compressed
   in full; h1 of E3 is read from the real compression, and the gate (4 conditions) and rule A (8 conditions) are
   evaluated on it.
2. Bitsliced program: one straight-line program over 256-bit slices computes X0, X10, C2 (a1, d1, c1, b1, a2), z and
   the gate and rule-A lane masks from the table slices XA[0..31], X6[0..31]. Every AND/OR/XOR on 256-bit words is one
   operation; rotations are free (renaming). Three designs:
     J  per-X2 code specialisation (JIT): all run-time constants folded into the code, slice polarities tracked,
        so XOR with a constant costs nothing and a constant addition costs 1-2 ops per bit.
     D  static code, constant additions dispatched per 8-bit chunk (computed jump, 2 units per chunk), every slice
        normalised to true polarity at the end of each chunk adder (one XOR with ONES per inverted slice).
     G  generic: constant bits are loaded slices (all-0 / all-1 words, precomputed per X2), no specialisation.
3. Register model: R regist

inventory.name: affine
inventory.description:
affine.py: can small-t cube members be ENUMERATED instead of filtered? (a push on the method's size limit)

Per outer step the map F: c1 -> t (the counter solved from E1.d1 = c1 - Y11) is a bijection built from three
rotations (16, 7, 8: net ROR 1), XORs with constants and four additions of constants. Over the T1 cube (11 fixed
bits, 21 free bits) it is close to affine over GF(2). The affine-guided enumerator:
  1. evaluate F at the cube's base point and at base XOR e_i for the 21 free bits: delta_i = F(base^e_i)^F(base)
     (22 evaluations, about 300 word ops);
  2. solve over GF(2): bits >= k of F(base) ^ sum x_i delta_i must be 0 (32 - k equations, 21 unknowns);
     inconsistent -> skip the outer step;
  3. enumerate the solution space (particular + null space), compute F exactly on each candidate, keep t < 2^k.
Ground truth: all t in [1, 2^k) inverted through F^-1 (exact list of cube members with small t).
Reported: fraction of outer steps flagged good vs actually good, recall (true hits found / all true hits),
candidates per hit (exact evaluations per kept trial).
usage: python -B affine.py NOUTER K SEED [NBASE]
(NBASE linearization points per outer step: the cube base point, then random cube members)

inventory.description:
outer_filter.py [OUTCOMES]   (counter_next/stack; research only)

EXACT share of outer steps that can contain a collision, for the counter arrangement (pin H8, 55/63, sub-class).
Per outer step the E3 inputs y = Y4, Q = Y9, W = w8 are fixed (only h1 moves); E = Y3 + y + w8, E' = E + DY3.
For an E1 outcome (beta, tau, eps) with n = 0, an E3 match needs (e3cond.py, checked on 200,000 real pairs):
  (1) exists h1:  (Q + h1) ^ (Q + (h1 ^ eta)) = G(tau),  G = ROL(tau ^ ROR(tau,1), 12)
  (2) exists f1:  (E + f1) ^ (E' + (f1 ^ ROR(G,12))) = eps
Both are properties of outer words only.  An outer step where, for every listed outcome, (1) or (2) has no solution
holds no trial with R = 0 of a listed outcome: skipping it loses no collision (exact, no model).
Counted exactly over all 2^32 Q and all 2^32 E by subset-construction DPs (state: the reachable carry pairs of the
existential word, per outcome).  Q and E are independent uniform words under M_outer (Sol answer Y section 7: Q = Y9 and
W = w8 are two of the seven independent outer words; E = Y3 + y + W), so
  P(pass) = sum over (solvable pattern a of Q, solvable pattern b of E) P(a) P(b) [a and b share an outcome].
OUTCOMES: 'bstar' (the 7 rows of beta*, default) or 'all' (every row of a15_outcomes.tsv with a nonzero product).

inventory.name: bit gd
inventory.description:
Bit-level guess-and-determine for the idea-1 systems (main session, Pivot, 2026-10-08; owner's "bigger cube" idea).

The word-level model (gd_order.py) treats each 32-bit word as one unit and needs exactly 4 checks (128 bits) per family
member for the fixed variant.  Here every word is split into its 32 bits, and every modular addition gets its carry
bits.  Structural rules only (no value-dependent shortcuts):
  - xor equations (sum bits, rotated-xor bits, fixed output xors): any one unknown bit is solved from the others;
  - carries: k[i+1] = maj(p[i], q[i], k[i]) is known once its three inputs are known (forward only); k[0] = 0.
A three-term addition z = p + q + x uses an intermediate word t = p + q.
checks (in bits) = guessed bits - family freedom in bits.  A member then costs about 2^checks trials.
Usage: python bit_gd.py <fixed|fixed13|outhalf|outhalf13> <runs> [seed]

inventory.name: bit kill
inventory.description:
ctr x join, part K: why screen-2 candidates die.

For every screen-2 candidate (U, V, surviving bits) of ctr_split_numeric.py, test each surviving
match bit b with 8 bases x 32 draws per side and record CROSS moves:
  V resample changes key1 bit b  or  U resample changes key3 bit b.
One cross move proves bit b is not split for that (U, V) (key1_b depends on V or key3_b on U).
Bits with no cross move are 'unrefuted'; for those, report how often key1_b and key3_b move at
all and P(key1_b == key3_b) over random trials (the most a join on that bit could save is
-log2 of that probability).

inventory.name: bit prune
inventory.description:
Bit-level pruning of word-level solving orders (main session, Pivot, 2026-10-08).

Start from a word-level covering guess set (8 words = 256 bits for the fixed variant), then try to drop guessed bits one
at a time: a bit may be dropped when propagation from the remaining guesses still determines every bit.  Repeated with
random drop orders and several starting orders.  checks (bits) = guessed bits left - 128.
Usage: python bit_prune.py <variant> <restarts> [seed]

inventory.name: bitgd
inventory.description:
Bit-level guess-and-determine for a ring subsystem (shape_torus, 2026-10-08).

Each 32-bit word is itself a ring Z/w of bits: a rotation is a shift around that ring, an addition is a carry
chain that runs one way (bit 0 -> bit w-1) and so CUTS the bit ring at bit 0.  A word-level ring closure
f(c) = c can be solved by seeding s bits and running around the bit ring; s is what this module estimates.

Input: word-level primitive equations (name, words) in the gd_order.py format, the set of UNKNOWN words
(everything else is known), word size w.  Roles (from the equation name):
  X:a1 / X:a2  out = in1 + in2 + in3       X:c1 / X:c2  out = in1 + in2
  X:d1 R0, X:b1 R1, X:d2 R2, X:b2 R3       out = ROR_R(in1 ^ in2)
  outN                                     w0 ^ w1 = const
Bit variables: word bits, carry bits, temp-word bits.  Bit equations:
  linear (xor of <= 4 bits = known): solves any one unknown;  carry c[i+1] = MAJ(x_i, y_i, c_i): forward only.
Seeds = guessed bits.  Propagation is exact (each step determines one bit uniquely from known ones), so
"seed s bits, propagate, test the unused equations" enumerates every root with 2^s passes.   [DERIVED]

inventory.name: build pkg5
inventory.description:
Render the fifth package from its templates and the one data place. Research helper, not submitted.

    python -B tools/build_pkg5.py            write the package files and the note
    python -B tools/build_pkg5.py --check    write nothing; say whether the files on disk are what the templates give

Templates (src/): proof_head.md (Sections 1 to 9), proof_evidence.md (Section 10), claim.json, manifest.json,
note.md. A template is the final text with {{name}} where a figure depends on the pinned call, the class or the
rate; the names are defined in tools/pkg5_data.py and nowhere else. Edit the text in src/, never in the rendered
files: a later build overwrites them (--check shows the difference first).

What the build does:
  1. writes the pin, eta and rule A of pkg5_data.py into experiments/halfsearch.py (five lines, with the stage-2 budget) and checks, by loading
     the program, that its class, its list, rule A and the stage counts are those of the data module;
  2. renders the proof; a paragraph or list item that contains a name, or a line over 79 characters, is wrapped
     again at 79; tables, displayed formulas and headings are left as they are;
  3. finds the line ranges of the rendered proof that claim.json cites and renders claim.json with them;
  4. renders the experiment manifest and the note;
  5. refuses to write if a name is unknown, a proof line is over 79 characters, a file is not ASCII, the JSON
     files do not parse or a field is longer than the schema a

inventory.name: certb verify
inventory.description:
certb_verify.py: referee recomputation of the single-centre success-probability inputs (proof.md section 8.7). Needs no data file except the organizer's constants JSON.
usage:  python certb_verify.py ORCHARD_CONSTANTS.json C0 L [J [C0A]]   (J = line index, default 0; C0A = the CERT A critical point, checked if given)
needs:  python 3 and python-flint (tested with 0.9.0: fmpz_mod_poly with pow_mod, compose_mod, gcd, derivative, pow_trunc, inverse_series_trunc)
V1  build F_j (degree 5^7) by evaluation at the 2^17-th roots of unity and one inverse transform; check F(tau^5) against an independent reference hash (5 values of tau).
V7  for m = 5, 25, ..., 15625: H_m is forced by the top m coefficients of F (r-th root series, r = 5^7 / m); F mod H_m must be non-constant (no right factor of degree m).
V6  (if C0A is given; CERT A) F'(C0A) = 0, F''(C0A) != 0, g(C0A; S) has constant term 0 and gcd(g, g') = 1.
V2  g = H(C0; S) monic of degree d = 39062 from F and C0 by one Taylor shift.   V3  gcd(g, g') = 1.   V4  L is prime and d/2 < L <= d - 3.
V5  R_0 = x^p mod g, R_i = R_(i-1) o R_(i-1) mod g, Q = x^(p^L) mod g by the binary chain; g_L = gcd(g, Q - x), g_1 = gcd(g, R_0 - x);
    accept iff deg g_L - deg g_1 = L; then f = g_L / g_1 is irreducible of degree L and divides g (proof.md Lemma 8.7.1).
It prints SHA-256 of f, of g / f and of R_i mod f (32-byte little-endian coefficients, constant term first), to be compared with the values stated in proof.md.

inventory.name: Check of Dong et al. CRYPTO 2021 eq. (9)/(10) (2021_427.txt lines 1321-1443).
inventory.description:
Check of Dong et al. CRYPTO 2021 eq. (9)/(10) (2021_427.txt lines 1321-1443).
All quantities in BITS here (cells of w bits -> multiply by w). n = h*w output bits,
T = t*w target bits, Dp/Dm = DoF+/DoF- bits, M = m*w filter bits (M <= T).
Paper (eq 9, table-building terms dropped):  cost = n/2 - min(Dp-T/2, Dm-T/2, M-T/2, T/2)
Derivation (lines 1335-1347): episodes E = 2^((n-T)/2 - (Dp+Dm-T)), per-episode
cost 2^Dp + 2^Dm + 2^(Dp+Dm-M) + 2^(Dp+Dm-T).  Requires E >= 1, i.e. Dp+Dm <= (n+T)/2.
Constrained optimum: pick a<=Dp, b<=Dm with a+b <= (n+T)/2, e = (n+T)/2 - a - b >= 0:
  cost = e + max(a, b, a+b-M, a+b-T).

chk38.c - check2-4: independent check of the scout2-4 (hole 4) relaxed-q3 measurement on the filed r38 package.
Written from vt38.py (constants via kexport.py -> k38.h), not from smc38r.c.  Differences from the scout's design:
relaxed rows use plain uniform proposals only (no stratified imposed/outside streams), resampling is systematic
(not multinomial), the RNG is xoshiro256** (not splitmix64), the look-ahead test steps the next row with a dummy
word instead of a difference formula, the schedule differences come from placeholder words W0..W7 with the right
differences, and every tail success is rebuilt and checked by a separate a..h 38-step compression.

  M  cells of row 16, the filed first row-17 test (E17^x against the program's 10-bit mask FT_ME/FT_VE),
     published modular differences of rows 17..23, collision after step 37
  H  cells of row 16, published modular differences of rows 17..23, collision after step 37
usage: chk38 MODE seed NP N17 N18 N19 N20 N21 N22 NT [sfsfile]

inventory.name: class loop
inventory.description:
One complete outer step as the algorithm runs it: the whole table once, then the batches of several values of X2.

    python -B work/tools/class_loop.py [more values of X2, default 3] [batches for each of them, default 3000]

writes work/evidence/class_loop.txt. Research helper, not submitted. It uses the program's own counted pieces:

  1. outer_step once, on one machine (one context drawn here);
  2. table_build for every one of the words of the list (18,725 for the sub-class), each on a new machine: the five lists of the table
     are allocated here in full (the program itself builds only the words of the batch it counts) and compared
     with table_row() of every member; the counts of all words are added up;
  3. middle_step, then packed_batch for ALL batches of that value of X2, each with the words of the table
     built in step 2, every lane checked as the program's batch_check checks it (against the complete digests of
     the lane's two real messages);
  4. middle_step again, several times in a row on the same memory, so that X2 goes up by one each time, and for
     each new value the given number of batches drawn at random, with the SAME table: this is the point of the
     arrangement, the table of an outer step serves every value of X2.

It then states the memory: the number of words of the table and of the static list as allocated here, their size
as 256-bit words, and the number of memory cells the pieces use.

CryptoMiniSat 5.11 IN-PROCESS through its C API (the installed libcryptominisat5.so via ctypes; nothing installed or
compiled): the cost of the solve call alone, with no process start and no parsing.  time.perf_counter_ns() is read
around one C call (ctypes adds about 1 us per call, included).  One thread.  Cycles = ns x 4.7 (Ryzen 9 7900X).

inventory.name: cnfgen
inventory.description:
Bit-level CNF for the family-sampler problem of toy 2-round BLAKE3 (word size w).

Given a target taken from a random message M0 (so a solution exists), find a message M with
  fixedA : E0/E2 inputs equal to M0's (Y0,Y5,Y10,Y15,Y2,Y7,Y8,Y13 and m1,m11,m9,m14)          (12w bits)
  plusA  : effective E0/E2 inputs equal: Y0+m1, Y5, Y10, Y15, m11, Y2+m9, Y7, Y8, Y13, m14       (10w bits)
  outhalfA: out0, out2, out5, out7 equal to M0's                                                  (4w bits)
  fixedB/plusB/outhalfB: the same for E1/E3 (out1,3,4,6)
Optional: --fix k  fixes k random message bits to M0's values (more fixed bits -> fewer solutions);
          --xor k  adds k random parity constraints over message bits (agreeing with M0) to pick a random member.
Writes DIMACS; --check <solver output> decodes the message and verifies with toyb3.
Usage: python cnfgen.py <variant> <w> <seed> <out.cnf> [--fix k] [--xor k] [--check sol.out]

inventory.name: cores
inventory.description:
Exact check-count facts for the sphere door (k of out0,2,5,7 held) in the word-level GD model.

LEMMA (DERIVED; brute-force checked in lemma.py): in the GD model (each equation solvable for any one unknown),
  min checks = min number of equations whose deletion leaves a hypergraph with an EMPTY 2-core
  (2-core = what remains after repeatedly removing a word that lies in exactly one remaining equation, together
  with that equation; guesses are NOT removed - they play no role).
  Proof sketch: in a 0-check order every equation solves a word that occurs in no earlier equation; the last
  core equation cannot do that, because each of its words lies in another (earlier) core equation.  Conversely
  an empty core gives the order (reverse peeling) and the guesses are the words never solved.
  So: non-empty core => at least 1 check, for EVERY guess set.

TABLE MODEL (permissive): any subset B of the live equations of ONE G call (every call treated as table-able,
  the held out-equations of that call allowed in B) may be removed when B has a perfect matching onto words that
  occur in no other live equation.  A real table step (or one of ../gd_promote.py's cycle macros) with 0 checks
  has such a matching (Hall: otherwise a subset of its equations over-determines its words = a check), so a
  non-empty permissive core => at least 1 check with any per-call tables.

inventory.name: count-cost e3rule
inventory.description:
count-cost reviewer: the exact probability, under the seven-word model, that a trial shows a listed partial E3
event AND satisfies the rule on h1. The GPU programs count this joint event on real trials; the package compares it
only with draws from the model. Here it is counted exactly, with a method written for this purpose.

    python -B count-cost_e3rule.py            (Windows Python with numpy; one thread; about a minute)

Partial E3 event of a pair (psi, eps): Y4 in the class, and for the words (Y4, h1, Y9, w8)
    f1 XOR f1' = psi   and   e2 XOR e2' = eps        (the first five assignments of E3 for A and B).
With e1 = Y3 + Y4, g1 = Y9 + h1, e2 = e1 + f1 + w8 the map (Y4, h1, Y9, w8) -> (e1, h1, g1, e2) is a bijection, and
    (g1 + dh) XOR g1 = ROL(psi, 12),   dh = (h1 XOR eta) - h1        (a function of the 13 bits of h1 on eta)
    (e2 + D) XOR e2 = eps,              D = DY3 + (f1 XOR psi) - f1,  f1 = ROR(Y4 XOR g1, 12).
For an addition x -> x + D with a prescribed XOR difference X the solutions x form a cube: the carry into bit i is
D_i XOR X_i, so D_0 = X_0, D_(i+1) XOR X_(i+1) = D_i wherever X_i = 0 (i < 31), and x_i = D_(i+1) XOR X_(i+1)
wherever X_i = 1 (i < 31); all other bits of x are free. So: for each of the 2^13 patterns of h1 on eta, g1 is
fixed on the bits of ROL(psi,12) below 31; for each such g1 pattern every member of the class is visited (arrays),
D is formed and the cube of e2 is counted. Nothing is sampled.

Checks: the cube rule against brute force

inventory.name: cube-index of c1 bits 9,10,11,12,13,14
inventory.description:
Exact neutrality test for c1 bits 11-14 vs full 2^21 brute force.

Model (DERIVED):
  d1 = c1 - Y11. Bits 9-14 of c1 are copied into d1 with carry 0
  (CY[9..14]=0 and cin into bit 9 is 0). Bit 15 is a constant kill.
  Flipping c1 bit p in {11,12,13,14} flips only a1 bit p+16, then a
  carry chain in y6 = a1 + q that stays inside bits p+16..31, which
  ROL-7 maps onto y10 bits (p-9)..6. y14 = y10 + (-C2.c1) then carries
  upward. y14 bits >= 8 change iff the carry into bit 8 changes, and
  the six HIGH rule-A conditions are functions of that carry together
  with background bits. The two LOW conditions (h1 bits 16 and 17,
  i.e. y14 bits 0 and 1) do not depend on c1 bits 11-14.
  The AND of the six high conditions cannot hold for both carry-in
  values (cond 0 or cond 6 always flips with that carry). So the pass
  flag changes under the flip iff some cube point with the low
  conditions true has the high AND true, and the flipped point has
  the other carry.

inventory.name: dds4
inventory.description:
DDS double-kernel family on SHA3-256 r6, middle placement: EXACT min of w(chi5) per mid by factor tables (COMPUTED).

w(L(b4)) = sum over chi5 rows R of W(value_R), value_R = XOR of the contributions of the chi4-output rows that touch R
(L is linear, so theta cancellations are included).  Each R is a factor over the few variables touching it;
the sum is accumulated on the full grid of variable choices with numpy broadcasting, chunked on leading variables.
Usage: python dds4.py <first_class> <last_class_exclusive> [max_vars_exact=14]
Appends per-class lines to dds4.txt and per-mid lines to dds4_mids.txt.

inventory.name: dds5
inventory.description:
DDS middle placement: achievable collision probability through chi5 + digest round (COMPUTED, linear algebra).

Given chi5 input difference a5, the chi5 output difference b5 is uniform on the affine space S(a5) (dim w(a5)).
The digest collides when every plane-0 chi6 row has an allowed input difference.  Relaxation used here
(sufficient, so it gives an ACHIEVABLE probability, i.e. an upper bound on the cost):
  bits x=0..3 of all 64 plane-0 chi6 rows are zero  -> probability 2^-r over b5 (r = rank, if consistent),
  then each plane-0 row with only its x=4 bit set costs 2 conditions (PD = 8/32);
  cost C_ub = r + 2*E|x4| (Jensen), E|x4| = (#constant-1 bits) + (#non-constant bits)/2.
Total over the b4 choices of a mid:  P = 2^-(w3+w4) * sum_b4 2^-C_ub(L(b4)).
Usage: python dds5.py <first_class> <last_class_exclusive> [max_w4=13]

inventory.name: dds6
inventory.description:
Why the digest round fails after the theta6 spread (COMPUTED diagnosis, exact).

For chi5 input difference a5, b5 ranges over S(a5).  Each plane-0 chi6 row value is an affine function of b5.
(i)  rows whose value is CONSTANT over S(a5) and not an allowed digest pattern -> P(collision | a5) = 0 exactly.
(ii) otherwise an exact depth-first search over the allowed row patterns with incremental GF(2) elimination
     decides feasibility (any b5 with every plane-0 row allowed), and returns the cheapest pattern cost found.
Usage: python dds6.py <first_class> <last_class_exclusive> [max_w4=13]

inventory.name: dds7
inventory.description:
Digest-round structure after the theta6 spread, DDS middle placement (COMPUTED, exact, no search).

For every class, every kernel-keeping mid with w(chi4) <= MAXW4 and every chi4 output b4:
  a5 = L(b4); the 64 plane-0 chi6 rows are affine functions of b5 in S(a5).
  const_bad : some plane-0 row is constant over S(a5) with a value that can never give a digest collision
              -> P(collision | a5) = 0 exactly.
  forced    : number of plane-0 rows whose x=0..3 part cannot be made zero by any b5 (each such row must take a

inventory.name: dp proof
inventory.description:
dp_proof.py (hotspot; research only) - EXACT carry counts (bit-serial dynamic programme) for the two strongest hot
spots, independent of any sampling.

E1 side. In the cube, c1b = c1 ^ CM (beta = beta*), and d2b = d2 ^ ror(tau, 8). So
    eps = (c1 + d2) ^ ((c1 ^ CM) + (d2 ^ ror(tau, 8)))
depends on (c1, d2) only. For each listed tau of beta*, count (c1 in the cube, d2 any 32-bit value) with eps = eps*,
split by the parities c1[11]^c1[12] and c1[20]^c1[22]. Every d2 value is reachable by some a2, so a zero count
means NO trial (any a1, Y6, w5, outer words) can give the listed E1 outcome in that cell.

E3 side. h1b = h1 ^ ETA (class), so Delta g1 = (y9 + h1) ^ (y9 + (h1 ^ ETA)) depends on (y9, h1) only, and the
listed partial E3 events of eps* need Delta f1 = ror(Delta g1, 12) in the eps* list. Count (y9, h1) per value of
(y9[0], y9[1], y9[2]); a zero count means no outer step with those Y9 bits can give such an event.

inventory.name: e3cond
inventory.description:
e3cond.py (counter_next/stack; research only)

The E3 side of a counter-arrangement trial, written as three exact XOR-difference conditions on one inner word.

Per outer step the counter arrangement fixes y = Y4, Q = Y9, W = w8 (Sol answer Y section 7: E3 coordinates (y,Q,W,h));
only h1 moves.  With E = Y3 + y + w8 and E' = Y3' + y + w8 = E + DY3 (exact), and E1 outcome (beta, tau, eps):
  R = 0  <=>  dE3.c = tau (word 1), dE3.a = eps (word 3), dE3.b = ROR(tau,8) (word 4), dE3.d = ROR(beta^eps,7) (word 6)
and with h1' = h1 ^ eta (class), f1 = ROR(y ^ g1, 12), e2 = E + f1, h2 = ROR(h1 ^ e2, 8), g2 = g1 + h2:
  (1) (Q + h1) ^ (Q + (h1 ^ eta)) = G   with G = ROL(tau ^ ROR(tau,1), 12)          [from words 1 and 4]
  (2) (E + f1) ^ (E' + (f1 ^ ROR(G,12))) = eps                                       [word 3]
  (3) (g1 + h2) ^ (g1' + h2') = tau,  h2 ^ h2' = ROR(eta ^ eps, 8)                   [word 1]
  word 6 needs n = eps ^ ROL(beta ^ eps, 1) ^ eta = 0 (Lemma N; E1 only).
Part A checks these identities on random real E3 executions (both messages).  Part B counts, exactly by carry DP over
one 32-bit word, the solutions of (1) for sampled Q and of (2) for sampled E, for the seven beta* outcomes, and the share
of outer steps for which (1) and (2) have no solution for any of the seven (such an outer step cannot contain a
collision of a beta* outcome: an EXACT necessary-condition filter on outer words).

In the counter arrangement the E3 inputs other than h1 are fixed per outer step: U = (y = Y4, Y9, w8)
(counter/structure cone: Y9, w8 do not move with the inner word), and the inner map c1 -> h1 is a permutation of
all 2^32 words (sol_answer_Y section 7.1).  E3 on A and B is then a function of h1 alone:
    e1 = Y3 + y, e1' = Y3' + y, h1' = h1 ^ eta,

R = 0 needs, for the outcome j = (beta, tau, eps) (beta is a function of eps by Lemma N):

breadth-first search over the bits of h1, low to high, checking each condition bit as soon as all the bits it reads

inventory.name: e3solve
inventory.description:
e3solve.py [SEED] [PLANTS] [STEPS]   (counter_next/stack; research only)

Prototype of an E3-first solve for one outer step of the counter arrangement: given (y, Q = Y9, W = w8), find EVERY
h1 in Z_2^32 for which E3 matches an outcome (G, eps, tau):  (1) dg1 = G, (2) de2 = eps, (3) dg2 = tau.
Method: enumerate the solutions f1 of (2) by a carry DFS pruned with a backward feasibility table (output-sensitive),
map f1 -> g1 = ROL(f1,12) ^ y -> h1 = g1 - Q, test (1), then run E3 on both messages and test (3).
Checks: (a) PLANTS random real E3 pairs, each pair's own differences as the target: its h1 must be among the solutions
(completeness); every returned h1 must satisfy all three conditions on a forward re-run (soundness).
(b) STEPS outer steps that pass the exact outer filter (outer_filter.py) for the beta* outcomes: number of f1
solutions enumerated, DFS nodes, survivors of (1), solutions of (1)-(3); an op count of the solve.

inventory.name: e3solve2
inventory.description:
e3solve2.py [SEED] [STEPS]   (counter_next/stack; research only)

Joint DFS for the E3-first solve: walk the bits of h1 from 0 to 31, carrying the (1)-automaton state (carries of
Q + h1 and Q + (h1 ^ eta)); g1 = Q + h1 is known bit by bit, and f1 bit k = (y ^ g1) bit k+12, so from bit 12 on
the (2)-automaton (carries of E + f1 and E' + f1') advances too; both are pruned by exact backward feasibility tables.
At the leaf the (2)-automaton finishes on f1 bits 20..31 = (y ^ g1) bits 0..11.  Output: all h1 with (1) and (2).
Checked against e3solve.py's solver (enumerate (2), filter by (1)) on the same passing outer steps: the two solution
sets must be equal.  Reports DFS nodes per passing step.

inventory.name: e3split
inventory.description:
e3split.py (counter_next/knobs; research only): a cheaper exact E3 search by splitting h1 at bit 12.

The bits of h1 below 12 reach the rest of E3 only through (i) the carry pair into bit 12 of g1 = Y9 + h1 and
g1' = Y9 + h1', (ii) g1 bits 0..11 (-> f1 bits 20..31 -> e2 bits 20..31), (iii) h1 bits 8..11 (-> h2 bits 0..3)
and (iv) g1 bits 0..11 in g2 = g1 + h2.  e2 bits 0..19 depend only on f1 bits 0..19 = (y ^ g1) bits 12..31 and
start with carry 0.  So, per target:
  LOW : all h1 bits 0..11 meeting dg1 bits 0..11, grouped by the carry pair into bit 12 (bit-serial search);
  HIGH: for each carry pair present, all h1 bits 12..31 meeting dg1 bits 12..31 and de2 bits 0..19 (bit-serial);
  JOIN: every (low, high) pair with the same carry pair -> full check of the four E3 differences.
Cost = nodes of LOW + nodes of HIGH + number of JOIN pairs (each a full E3 evaluation, about 30 operations).
Checked against e3dfs.search (plain search, itself checked against the 2^32 brute force) on planted and random
outer steps.
usage: python -B e3split.py check NU SEED   |   python -B e3split.py cost NU SEED NT

L1  For a fixed G input (a,b,c,d), the maps (x,y) -> (a2,d2) and (x,y) -> (b2,c2) are bijections.

inventory.name: exact routes
inventory.description:
Exact linear-consistency filter for word-level message-only routes (one process, capped).

The truncated model (trunc_search.c) treats every cancellation as possible.  Here every word also
carries its modular difference as a linear form over GF(p) (p = 2^61-1, a proxy for the integers):
  - message word m_j: its own variable (the SAME variable in round 0 and round 1);
  - an addition: the exact sum of its input forms; a cancellation adds the constraint "sum = 0";
  - an xor-rotate output: a fresh variable (no linear relation assumed: optimistic);
  - every active value must stay nonzero (not forced to 0 by the constraints).
A route is linearly infeasible when the constraints force an active value to 0.

Refined round-1 cost (model B'): xor cancellations and fold cancellations count 1; an addition
cancellation counts 1 when its reduced constraint involves a fresh variable (a condition on values),
0 when it only relates message differences (a free choice of differences) or is already implied.

Search: depth-first over the 16 G calls and all op-level cancellation choices, pruned by the exact
truncated model-B cost-to-go (round-0 conditions free, round-1 + fold counted) and by linear
infeasibility.  So it is exhaustive over routes whose truncated model-B cost is <= budget.

  python -B exact_routes.py <M> <budget> [node_cap]

inventory.description:
s3-2block-capacity / experiment_C2.py  (exact-form version)
2-round and 3-round affine field dimension vs block-2 capacity, via EXACT polarization forms.

Round 1 is affine for ANY source direction and ANY capacity (origin_test k=1). So F2 is degree 2 on the whole
320-bit source; its polarization B2(a,b) = cube-sum over {a,b} is a GF(2)-bilinear form valued in GF(2)^1600.
A 2-round-affine field = max totally-isotropic subspace of B2 (isotropic for all 1600 scalar forms at once).
  - radical(B2) = {a : B2(a,.)=0 for all output bits}   (rigorous lower bound on the 2-round field)
  - maximal isotropic subspace (greedy grow by null-space)  (the 2-round field dimension)
At cap 0 this reproduces W40 (dim 40). Within the 2-round field V, F3=chi3 o affine is degree 2; its polarization
B3 on a basis of V gives the 3-round field = max isotropic of B3|V (cap 0 -> matches linstruct3 = 2).

Usage: python experiment_C2.py CAPMODE ORDERINGS     (CAPMODE: zero | cap<seed> | full<seed>)

inventory.name: experiment D
inventory.description:
s3-2block-capacity / experiment_D.py
Reliable, capacity-dependent replica of linstruct3's obstruction metric, at every round depth.

For round depth k, two source directions a,b are "k-round-compatible on a coset" iff the cube-sum (2nd finite
difference) of F_k over {a,b} is zero. A k-round-affine FIELD requires all its pairs compatible (necessary;
for k>=3 F_k has degree>2 on the full source, so we require compatibility at SEVERAL random cosets t -> a
direction pair that is affine on all tested cosets). We build the compatibility graph over the 320 source
coordinate directions and report: #compatible pairs, #triangles (trace(A^3)/6, exact), greedy max clique.
linstruct3's whole result was "max clique 2 / 0 triangles" at capacity 0. If a bought capacity raises the
triangle/clique count at k=3, a 3-round field of dim>=3 opens.

Everything uses the organizer round function cd.rnd (validated vs keccak.py permutation on nonzero capacity).
Usage: python experiment_D.py KDEPTHS(e.g. 2,3,4) NBASES NRANDCAPS

inventory.name: g1feas
inventory.description:
g1feas.py (counter_next/knobs; research only): an outer-step filter for the EXISTING cube program.

In the counter arrangement Y9 is fixed per outer step, and a success with outcome j needs
g1 ^ g1' = ROL(tau_j ^ ROR(tau_j, 1), 12) with g1 = Y9 + h1, h1' = h1 ^ eta.  If no h1 at all meets that for any
of the seven beta* outcomes, the outer step cannot succeed and its 2^21-trial cube loop can be skipped.
This measures the share of uniform Y9 for which the condition is feasible for at least one beta* outcome (exact
carry-pair automaton per Y9), and checks the claim 'infeasible => no success' on the exact counts' own terms:
the outcomes' E3 counts N_j are sums over Y9, so their whole mass lies on feasible Y9 (DERIVED).
usage: python -B g1feas.py NY9 SEED

inventory.name: gd
inventory.description:
b3-r1c scout: word-level guess-and-determine (GD) search on the 2-round pair system.

Each G call is 8 word relations (a1=a+b+x, d1=ror(d^a1,16), c1=c+d1, b1=ror(b^c1,12),
a2=a1+b1+y, d2=ror(d1^a2,8), c2=c1+d2, b2=ror(b1^c2,7)); any single unknown word in a
relation is determined by the others.  A relation whose words all become known without
being used is a check (a 32-bit filter).  Dimension = guesses - checks (in words).  The
cost of a GD order is 2^(32*peak dimension) candidates.  Search: iterative deepening on
the peak with memoisation on the known set.

Message pair A only (B follows: same X by Lemma L, pins hold for both).

inventory.name: gd order
inventory.description:
Guess-and-determine search for a solving order of 2-round BLAKE3 (single block, fixed IV).

Each G call is split into its eight primitive equations; each primitive equation links 3 or 4 words and can be
solved for any one of them once the others are known (additions and xor-rotations are invertible in each
argument).  Given the constants (IV, counter, length, flags, the fixed message words and the fixed internal words
of the chosen variant), find the fewest words to guess so that propagation determines everything.

checks = guesses - freedom.  A sampler with checks == 0 produces one family member per guess at O(1) cost.
Variants:
  fixed   : inputs of E0 and E2 fixed (Y0,Y5,Y10,Y15,Y2,Y7,Y8,Y13 and m1,m11,m9,m14)
  outhalf : only out0,out2,out5,out7 fixed (E0 and E2 included; out_i = v_i ^ v_{i+8})
Usage: python gd_order.py [fixed|outhalf] [len64|len55] [runs]

inventory.name: gd promote
inventory.description:
Solving-order search with precomputed tables and promoted constants (main session, Pivot, 2026-10-08). Memory is free and preprocessing up to ~2^85 is negligible in this cost model, so a G call whose external words include k family constants has 6 - k degrees of freedom; when 6 - k <= 2, ANY 6 - k known words of it determine the rest through a table of at most 2^64 entries built once per family (enumerate the free words, store by the known ones). Special cycles with constant parameters (C0/C2: input c -> d1; C1/C3: input b -> c1) are kept. "Promoting" p words makes them constants of a sub-family: the sub-family keeps 4 - p words of freedom (fixed variant), and the extra constants may turn more calls into table lookups. checks = min guesses - (4 - p). A sub-family of 2^64 members (p = 2) is enough for the birthday. Usage: python gd_promote.py

[pool: msg|msgX]

inventory.name: gd sat
inventory.description:
Exact minimum guess basis for the solving-order problem of gd_order.py, by SAT.

known[v][t]: word v is known after t propagation layers.  known[v][0] <-> guessed or constant.
known[v][t+1] -> known[v][t] or (some equation containing v has every other word known at t).
All words known at layer T; at most k guesses (sequential counter).
Writes DIMACS for each k; run a solver on it; decode with --decode <cnf> <solver output>.
Usage: python gd_sat.py <fixed|outhalf> <len64|len55> <k> [T]

inventory.name: gd sphere
inventory.description:
Sphere / nested (fractal) families in the word-level guess-and-determine model of ../gd_order.py.

Sphere: instead of holding the whole half-digest (out0,2,5,7) constant, hold only a subset S of its 4 words
(outhalf variant with |S| output equations), or hold only some of the 12 E0/E2 input words (fixed variant with
r words released).  The half-digest then spreads over 2^h values, h = 32*(4-|S|) resp. h <= 32*r, and the
birthday needs 2^((128+h)/2) members.  Nested: the levels |S| = 1,2,3,4 are families inside families.
checks = min guesses - freedom (greedy upper bound; with or without the table macros of ../gd_promote.py).
Projected exponent (log2 units, before word-op discounts) = (128 + h)/2 + 32 * checks.
Usage: python gd_sphere.py outhalf <runs> | python gd_sphere.py fixed <runs> <rmax>

inventory.name: gd two
inventory.description:
Two-block combined model (variant e, 'two-level'): block 1 is a full 2-round compression with all 16 message
words free (IV, counter 0, len 64, flags CHUNK_START); its chaining value o_i = v_i ^ v_{i+8} (i<8) feeds block 2,

inventory.name: gd var
inventory.description:
Guess-and-determine model for variants of the 2-round BLAKE3 family question (base: ../gd_order.py).

Word-level model: every G call is 8 primitive equations, each solvable for any one of its words.
Options
  half    02 : family holds E0,E2 side (out0,2,5,7)     13 : E1,E3 side (out1,3,4,6)
  mode    fixed   : all 12 input words of the two E calls are constants
          outhalf : the two E calls are modelled; only their 4 output words (out_i = v_i ^ v_{i+8}) are held
          partial : only the input words listed in `held` are constants (the rest of the 12 are free)
  length  64 or 55 (55: m14, m15 constant zero; m13's zero top byte is NOT modelled, treated as free)
  cvvar   chaining value words init0..init7 are unknowns (two-block, CV varying inside the family)

inventory.name: gdcv
inventory.description:
Table-backed chaining value (two-block messages), guess-and-determine model.

Block 2 of a 2-block message starts from v0..v7 = CV = first 8 output words of block 1 (flags CHUNK_START);
v8..v15 are constants (IV0..3, counter 0, block length, flags CHUNK_END|ROOT).  Memory is free and 2^(32t)
preprocessing is cheap for t <= 2 (2^64) or t = 2.75 (2^88): hash 2^(32t) random first blocks and index the CVs
by any t chosen CV words.  Then 'any t CV words known -> all 8 CV words known' (one lookup, ~1 hit expected).
So the CV is a block of 8 unknown words with dimension t: rules {p,q} -> r for every pair p,q (t = 2).
freedom = (unknowns - equations) - (8 - t).
Usage: python gdcv.py <gdv variant> [runs] [seed] [t=2] [--export]

inventory.name: gdcv
inventory.description:
Two-block "CV list" staged search (variant e).  The chaining value words (init0..init7) are unknowns that come
from a precomputed list of first blocks.  Phase 1: guesses B (non-CV words) propagate WITHOUT any equation that
contains a CV word.  Keys: CV equations whose non-CV words are all known after phase 1 (each a 32-bit lookup key
on the CV list).  Phase 2: all CV words known (list entry), full propagation must reach everything.
checks c = |B| - Ffixed; keys J <= c; post-filter checks c - J.
Model file as for gdx plus a line "cv cnt i1..icnt" (indices of the CV words) after the reps line; reps must not
contain CV words.   usage: gdcv model k Ffixed proc nprocs maxprint [slack: also count leaves with J >= c - slack]

inventory.name: gdtab
inventory.description:
Free-memory tables of whole G calls (2^64 entries, 2^64 preprocessing each).

A G call whose four state INPUTS are family constants (K calls) or whose four state OUTPUTS are family constants
(E0, E2 in the 'eout' variant) is a 2-dimensional relation in its six free ports (x, y and the four other state
words): tabulate it over its two free dimensions (2^64 entries) and any 2 known ports give the other 4 (one
lookup, ~1 solution expected).  Calls with one more constant port (e.g. K0 with m1 fixed) are 1-dimensional:
any 1 known port gives the rest (2^32 table).  Rules {p,q} -> r (or {p} -> r) are added to the plain model.
Usage: python gdtab.py <gdv variant> [runs] [seed] [--export] [--cv]
  --cv : also the table-backed chaining value of gdcv.py (2-block message)

inventory.description:
gen.c - samples of the front-line residual of 2-round BLAKE3 (pkgCG family: frontline.py step CO + step CT).
One sample = 7 outer words (C0.d1 D2.a1 D2.b1 S11 S4 X9 w6), member k (19 bits, Y4 = e1 - Y3), cube index j
(21 bits, E1.c1 = 02008000 | pdep(j, ~0e09818b)). Blocks A (55 bytes) and B (63 bytes) at counter t, flags 3,
both compressed with a plain 2-round BLAKE3 compression. Digest words 0,2,5,7 are equal for every sample;
the residual R = digest words (1,3,4,6) XOR = K1 XOR K3 (sol_answer_D5_split.md section 1).
  gen rand <outdir> <N> <seed>            N independent samples (fresh outer words, k, j each)
  gen ctx  <outdir> <C> <Mk> <Jc> <seed>  C contexts x Mk members x Jc cube indices (random, with replacement)
Files written in <outdir> (little-endian u32, row-major, one row per sample):
  inputs.u32  12: ow0..ow6, k, j, Y4, c1, t
  einputs.u32  9: Y1 Y6 Y12 w12 w5 | Y4 Y9 Y14 w8        (side A; side B differs only by Y3', Y11', w4', w5+DELTA5)
  dig.u32      8: digest A words 1,3,4,6 | digest B words 1,3,4,6
  eout.u32    16: E1 A (a2 b2 c2 d2) | E1 B | E3 A (e2 f2 g2 h2) | E3 B   (round-2 diagonal outputs)
  emid.u32    16: E1 A (a1 b1 c1 d1) | E1 B | E3 A (e1 f1 g1 h1) | E3 B   (half-G values)
  keys.u32     8: K1 (1,3,4,6) | K3 (1,3,4,6)
  res.u32      4: R (1,3,4,6)

inventory.name: gen batch2
inventory.description:
Batch instances, LAYOUT 2 (the production layout of the t1filter solver).
Free-word coordinates B2 = (D2.b1, K3.d1, S15, X4 | D3.a1, K0.b1), loop variable g = C0.b1 (valid k=1 design on the exact
relation set, same 21-equation loop and same 14 loop parameters as split_e3/ev.py DESIGN; design2.py).
A BATCH holds E3 = (Y4,Y9,w8) and D2.b1, K3.d1, S15, X4; the two words D3.a1, K0.b1 vary per proposal (2^64 proposals per
batch).  Then the table inputs Y4, X4, X8, w6, S11 (and X13) are batch constants (asserted); w5 = f(S14) varies.
Batch kinds:
  N : E3 + held words from a real point (ev.real_point, T1 = 0); proposal 0 is the real point (root with T1 = 0, must
      NOT be returned); other proposals random (D3.a1, K0.b1).
  R : E3 from a real point; held words random; proposals random.
  P : planted: basis words random except Y4 from a real point (keeps the E3 class), T1 = t uniform in [1,2^19),
      triangular propagation on the exact relations; proposal 0 is that point (root with T1 = t).
Outputs as gen_batch.py; the json 'B' field holds the ORIGINAL design's six B words (for compare.py / ev.Design.run).
usage: python gen_batch2.py <tag> <nN> <nR> <nP> <per_batch> <seed>

Generates ntt_big.h: straight-line register-block kernels for the large transforms (ntt.c, 'big' plans).
usage: python3 gen_big.py KG KFMIN KFMAX
A big plan (a = KG + kf, KFMIN <= kf <= KFMAX) is run in two passes: a first pass of KG layers (blocks of 2^KG data words) and a last pass of
kf layers (blocks of 2^kf words, stride 1, the pass that is fused with the pointwise product).  Every kernel is straight-line text: no loop, no
branch, every register is a literal index x[n] of the register file RF.  Every statement that executes loads, stores, address or control
operations carries its charge on the same line (LD / ST / CTL); the field operations are charged by pallas.c (fp_bf and the others perform
exactly the three, two, three and two field operations written in their definitions).

inventory.name: gen step1
inventory.description:
Step-1 (dense part) CNF for the 38-step SHA-256 characteristic of ePrint 2026/1120 (scout2-1, research only).

Unknowns: A0..A15, E4..E15, W8..W15 of member x; member y = x XOR the Table-3 differences (shared literals).

inventory.description:
heur.py  (untried/b3-heur; research only; run inside WSL Ubuntu, one CPU process at a time)

Non-gradient heuristic for the class choice of E3 (layer r1d, free const, counter base): simulated annealing over
ONE member e1 = Y3 + Y4 (Y4 is an outer word on the counter path, so one member is enough), scored by the team's
exact counter tool pair_calc_sub (beta* = 18b0e098 alone, pin H8; the same call as counter_next/stack/run_cube.sh with
-cube ffffffff e1).  Per-member rates (normalisation of scan_y4.py, free = 0):
    total = sum_j L_j N_j / 2^64  over every row      (the objective of the stack's greedy scan; best known 76,161,024)
    S     = the same sum over the six front-line taus  (class value 67,633,152, the map's Section 2.6 figure)
Phase A: e1 inside the front-line class (e1 AND 03cf8303) = 030c0303, 19 free bits, eta = 830303cf.
Phase B: all 32 bits of e1 free; eta = ROR(e1 XOR (e1 + DY3), 16) is recomputed per point, so every point is a valid
         member of its own class (a different class choice whenever a class-fixed bit flips).
Energy = -score, score = log2(S) * 64 + log2(total) in phase A (lexicographic: S first, total breaks ties) and
score = log2(total) in phase B.  Geometric temperature, 1-3 bit flips, restart after a stall.
Usage: python3 heur.py SECONDS SEED [PHASE_A_SHARE]
