inventory.name: identities
inventory.description:
Exact rotational-XOR identities of the residual, checked on every row of rand/ and ctx/.

Notation (XOR differences A^B): K1 = (da2, dc2, dd2, db2), K3 = (dg2, de2, df2, dh2) on digest words (1,3,4,6);
R = K1 ^ K3.  From the G steps (DERIVED): dd2 = ROR(da2,8) (d1 common), db2 = ROR(db1 ^ dc2, 7),
dh2 = ROR(eta ^ de2, 8) (dh1 = eta), df2 = ROR(df1 ^ dg2, 7); db1 = 18b0e098 and eta = 830303cf are constants here.
Rotational coordinates of R:
  U6 = R6 ^ ROR(R3,8) = ROR(db1,7) ^ ROR(eta,8) ^ ROR(dc2,7) ^ ROR(dc2,8)      (E1 only)
  W3 = R3 ^ ROL(R6,7) = db1 ^ ROR(eta,1) ^ de2 ^ ROR(de2,1)                     (E3 only)
  U4 = R4 ^ ROR(R1,8) = ROR(df1 ^ dg2 ^ ROR(dg2,1), 7)                          (E3 only)
  W4 = R4 ^ ROR(R1,7) = ROR(da2,8) ^ ROR(da2,7) ^ ROR(df1,7)                    (da2 from E1, df1 from E3)
Consequences: parity(R3) = parity(R6) on every row (parity(U6) = parity(db1) ^ parity(eta) = 0), so R lies in a
127-dimensional subspace; U6 = 0 <=> dc2 in {eps, ~eps}; W3 = 0 <=> de2 in {eps, ~eps}; W4 = 0 <=> df1 = da2 ^ ROR(da2,1).

inventory.name: idiff chain
inventory.description:
Step 3: how many rounds can the internal difference be kept DETERMINISTIC (constant) inside a symmetric field by
linear conditions alone, and what is left?  For a space t + span(B) (t p-periodic):
  round r: test whether delta_r = S_r xor rot_p(S_r) is affine on t + span(B) (64 random second differences);
           if affine: rank of its linear part = number of linear conditions; restrict B to the kernel (delta_r is then
           the constant delta_r(t) on the new coset); record weights; continue with round r+1.
           if not affine: the deterministic chain stops; record where.
Then sample NSAMP random points of the final coset and of the starting space and record the weight of delta_r per round
(rounds 1-5 full 1600-bit state, round 6 the 256-bit digest), against the random-state mean.
Usage: python idiff_chain.py SEED NT NSAMP SPACES(comma)   (spaces as in idiff_degree.py, no W40)

inventory.name: judge h3
inventory.description:
Hostile-judge lens: heuristic H3 of pkg5 over many sets of seed words, in the layout of proof.md 6.4. CPU only.

    python3 -B judge_h3.py SEEDS LOG2_BATCHES WORKERS [FIRST]

H3 says that no run has a share of trials that satisfy rule A as large as 9,363 * 2^85 / 2^104 = 2^-5.807 (1.1429 times
2^-6), so that at most one eighth of the batches run stage 2. The package supports it with four runs (four sets of
seed words) of 2^38 trials in a layout that leaves X13 unrestricted and X10 random. This program takes many sets of
seed words and, for each, a random sample of batches of the run that 6.4 defines for it:

    seed words X2, X5, X6, X9 (from SHAKE-256 of the seed number), X1 = X10 = 0,
    context X12 < 2^8, X13 < 2^16, X14 any; alpha any; batch j of the 9,363 batches of the class; its seven lanes.

For every lane it computes the trial of 6.1 as far as C2 with numpy (32-bit arithmetic), h1 = ROR(Y14 XOR (Y3 + Y4), 16)
and rule A as written in 6.3. Contexts, alphas and batches are sampled, not enumerated. As a check of this file, for
the first CHECK lanes of every worker h1 is compared with halfsearch.reference(), which builds the two real messages of
the trial and compresses them in full. Output: review/judge_h3_<SEEDS>_<LOG2_BATCHES>_<FIRST>.out (one line per seed
set and a summary). Nothing of the package is written.

inventory.description:

inventory.name: judge sat
inventory.description:
Hostile-judge lens: rule A against the E3 system of every outcome, with an encoder and a solver that are not
the package's. Read-only for the package; output review/judge_sat_<solver>.out. CPU only, at most 5 threads.

    python3 -B judge_sat.py cadical|cryptominisat5 [threads]

Written from proof.md alone (6.2, 6.3, Section 10 "How r is counted"): unknowns Y4, Y9, Y14, w8; E3 on message A is
G(Y3, Y4, Y9, Y14, 0, w8) and on message B is G(Y3', Y4, Y9, Y14, 0, w8). An outcome (beta, tau, eps) asks for
    h1 XOR h1' = eta                (Y4 in the class)
    g2 XOR g2' = tau                (c output of E3, residual word 1 against E1's a output)
    e2 XOR e2' = eps                (a output of E3, residual word 2 against E1's c output)
    f2 XOR f2' = ROR(tau, 8)        (b output of E3, residual word 3 against E1's d output)
    h2 XOR h2' = ROR(beta XOR eps, 7)   (d output of E3, residual word 4 against E1's b output)
This differs from the package's encoder in the unknown (Y14 instead of h1), in the conditions (the four output
differences of the residual instead of the differences of e1, g1, e2, g2) and in the adder clauses. Questions:
    base     the system                              expected SAT
    violate  the system AND h1 violates rule A       UNSAT means every solution of the outcome satisfies rule A
The outcomes are the OUTX lines of evidence/pairs_recount_e7c1815f.txt. Every model is evaluated in plain arithmetic.

inventory.name: kmerge
inventory.description:
k-list merge (Wagner k-tree, many solutions) on random lists, mixed xor / modular-add coordinates.

Toy group G = product of c coordinates of w bits, each 'add' (Z/2^w) or 'xor' ((Z/2)^w).  n = c*w.
Leaves = random lists (random function of the side's guess value).  A join node matches, per coordinate,
a number of LOW bits (low bits of a modular sum depend only on low bits of the summands, so this is exact for
'add'; for 'xor' any bits would do).  Goal: tuples with sum = 0 in G.

Cost counted in element-steps: build (leaf elements computed), ins (table inserts), look (streamed lookups),
out (elements produced at every join node, root outputs = solutions).  Predicted = the same recursion on
expected sizes (prod of leaf sizes / 2^matched bits), plus the closed forms written in RESULTS.txt.

inventory.name: ksat
inventory.description:
Exact word-level tests on the own model (wmodel.py), by SAT (kissat in WSL), over ALL guess sets (basis-free):
  min  : least guess-set size K whose propagation closure is every word; k = K - DOF.
  mitm : two-list meet in the middle. Fixed set A, side words P and Q; closure(A+P) and closure(A+Q) must together cover
         every core word (all k conditions are then side filters or matches).  |A|+|P|+|Q| = DOF+k, |P|,|Q| >= k.
         Per root it costs about 2^(32k+1)/N list entries with N <= 2^(32 min(|P|,|Q|)); this beats the bar only if such
         a cover exists for k = 1 (|P|,|Q| >= 1) or k = 2 (|P|,|Q| >= 2).
The model is first pruned to its core: a relation holding a word that appears nowhere else only defines that word
(an output computed after the solve) and is removed with it; DOF is unchanged.
usage: python ksat.py <counter> min <K>   |   python ksat.py <counter> mitm <k>

inventory.name: lane bound
inventory.description:
Largest lane value of every SUM of the two-stage batch of pkg6, per part, for ALL inputs, by interval arithmetic.

The self-test of the program reports the largest lane of a sum that occurred in its random cases. This tool runs
the same function packed_batch of experiments/halfsearch.py on a second machine that holds, for every register,
not a value but an upper bound of its lanes, and so gives a bound that holds for every context and every member:

  - a loaded word whose lanes are below 2^32 (a constant of the batch, a list word) counts as 2^32 - 1 in every
    lane, whatever its value; the word "bit 32" and the two counters are taken as they are;
  - a sum is bounded by the sum of the bounds of its operands;
  - an XOR is bounded bit by bit: below 2^32 it can be anything, above bit 31 it has at most the bits that one of
    the operands can have;
  - an AND with a loaded constant is bounded by the largest lane of that constant, a shift by 2^36 - 1 (bits of the
    neighbouring lane come in; every shift of the batch is followed by an AND with a loaded mask);
  - an OR is bounded by the all-ones word of the longer operand.

It prints, per part, the largest bound of a sum in units of 2^32 next to the bound of the program's TABLE, the
largest bound of all, and the largest bound of a word that enters the flag computation (it must be below 2^32).
It then runs the program's own machine on random batches and checks that every sum that occurs is at most the
bound found here. Nothin

inventory.name: lbsat
inventory.description: Exact lower bound on the free width of ANY binary join tree, by SAT (shape_any agent). Fact (DERIVED): in a rooted binary tree with E equation leaves, for every 2 <= k <= E/2 some internal node t has k <= |A_t| < 2k (walk the heavy path); its list pi_{B(A_t)} Sol(A_t) must be built, so width >= LB(k) = min_{k <= |A| < 2k} rho(A, B(A)), rho(A, Z) = min_{Z <= Y} |Y| - e_A(Y). With P promoted words (any choice, dependent or not) the bound uses cost |Y \ P| (a valid lower bound). Query: is there A, Y (and P) with cost <= T? UNSAT -> LB(k) > T. Usage: python lbsat.py

inventory.name: lbsat2
inventory.description:
Lower bound on the free width of ANY binary join tree when promoted constants may be chosen freely, limited by
the slack they consume (shape_any agent).

slack(P) = F - F'(P) = |P| - E + maxmatch(equations, words \ P)   (generic dimension lost by fixing P)
slack(P) <= S  <=>  there is a vertex cover (Konig) C_E + C_V of the bipartite graph eq--(word not in P) with
                   |P| + |C_E| + |C_V| <= S + E.
Cut part as in lbsat.py: A (k <= |A| < 2k), Y >= B(A) minus P, cost |Y \ P| - #{e in A : vars(e) <= Y u P} <= T.
(Equations lying inside P are counted as conditions: this can only lower the cost, so UNSAT stays a valid bound.)
Usage: python lbsat2.py <sys> <k> <T> <S> <out.cnf>

inventory.name: lbsat3
inventory.description:
Lower bound on the free width of ANY binary join tree (DP over any shape), with promoted constants chosen
freely up to a slack budget S (shape_any agent).  Refines lbsat2.py: the size window counts only equations that
still contain an unknown word after promotion (r_e), as in the propagated sub-family system.

  slack(P) = |P| - E + maxmatch(eq, words \ P) <= S   <=> vertex cover C with |P| + |C| <= S + E   (Konig)
  window   : k <= #{e in A : r_e} < 2k,   r_e = OR_{v in e} not p_v
  cost     : |Y \ P| - #{e in A : vars(e) <= Y u P} <= T,  Y >= B(A) \ P
UNSAT => for every promotion set with slack <= S and every tree on the remaining equations having a node in the
window (true when the remaining system has >= 2k equations; checked by mode 'drop'), width > T.

Usage: python lbsat3.py cut  <sys> <k> <T> <S> <out.cnf>
       python lbsat3.py drop <sys> <D> <S> <out.cnf>      (SAT iff slack <= S can remove >= D equations)

inventory.name: lbsat4
inventory.description:
Same lower-bound query as lbsat3.py, encoded with totalizers (unary counters) instead of sequential counters.
cost: sum q_v <= T + sum c_e is encoded as  Q >= T + j + 1  ->  C >= j + 1  between two unary counters.
Usage: python lbsat4.py cut  <sys> <k> <T> <S> <out.cnf> [letters]
       python lbsat4.py drop <sys> <D> <S> <out.cnf> [letters]

inventory.name: lbsat5
inventory.description:
Lower bound on the free width of ANY join tree with promotions (slack <= S), window RELATIVE to the number R of
equations that keep an unknown after promotion:  R/3 <= |A n remaining| < 2R/3   (shape_any agent).
Validity (DERIVED): with k = R/3 the heavy path of any tree over the R remaining equations has a node of
size in [k, 2k) = [R/3, 2R/3); no separate drop check is needed.  Optional letters: count only equations of
those G calls (weights), both in R and in the window.
Usage: python lbsat5.py <sys> <T> <S> <out.cnf> [letters]

legal.py - is a chunk counter t >= 2^32 legal for blake3-r2-prefix-v1, and what does hashing such a message cost?

inventory.name: lemma
inventory.description:
Brute-force check of the lemma used in cores.py, on random small hypergraphs.

A = exact minimum checks of the GD process (try every guess set of every size, propagate "equation with one
    unknown -> solve it", stop at the first size that determines every word; checks = size - (words - eqs)).

inventory.name: linearity of the difference map on random combinations
inventory.description:
Home-run trail door, step 1: the fixed difference after the two affine rounds of the W40 field, and its chi3-input image.
For each field direction w_i: D_i(x) = R1(R0(x)) xor R1(R0(x xor w_i)) (state after round index 1, organizer round function via
cube_degree.py). On every coset the map is affine, so D_i(x) must not depend on x - checked on many random x. Linearity of the
difference map (D(w_i xor w_j) = D_i xor D_j) checked on random combinations. Then B3_i = theta/rho/pi of round index 2 applied to
D_i (linear; constants cancel in differences) = the chi3 input difference. Writes l2_b3.bin (40 x 25 u64, little endian) and
prints the per-direction chi3 active-row counts. Usage: python step1_l2.py

inventory.name: model
inventory.description:
Part 2a: own word-level model of the 55/63 construction and own basis test (no SAT, no team code).

Model: every G assignment is one equation over the unknown words it contains; each equation can be solved
for any one of its unknowns (all are bijective in each argument).  E1/E3 first halves are modelled with the
pinned Y11, Y3, w15 substituted (c1 = Y11 + d1, e1 = Y3 + Y4).  Constants: IV, block length, flags, the pins
X3 X7 X11 X15 w4 w13 w15 (and w14 unless --w14free), hence all of K2's first four values and C3 entirely.
Counter: K0's d input is v12 = T0, K1's d input is v13 = T1; COUNTER=0: both constant 0; 1: T0 unknown;
2: T0 and T1 unknown.

Basis test.  B (|B| = n - m) is a triangular basis iff forward propagation from B determines every word.
Existence of a basis containing a forced set F is decided by REVERSE PEELING: repeatedly delete an equation
that owns a word not in F occurring in no other remaining equation.  Peeling is monotone (a private word stays
private when other equations are deleted), so greedy peeling succeeds iff some order does (proof in
STRUCTURE.md); success <=> a basis containing F exists, and the peeling gives the order (reversed) and the
basis (unclaimed words).  validate() checks this against brute force on random small systems.

inventory.name: neutral
inventory.description:
Bit-level, basis-free test for cheap E3-holding moves (neutral bits), on the own model (b3.py).
Free input bits: T0, m0 m1 m2 m3 m5 m6 m7 m9 m10 m11 m12 (12 words = 384 bits) and, for counter 2, T1 bits 0..18.
Held: pins X3 X7 X11 X15 and E3 inputs Y4 Y9 Y14 (224 bits); m4 m13 m8 m14 m15 are constants (no difference).
XOR-linear model: every modular addition replaced by XOR (rotations and XORs are exact).  A move delta keeps every held
word exactly when it is in the kernel of the held-word map AND every addition that feeds a held word behaves linearly;
for z = x + y with input XOR differences (alpha, beta) that has probability 2^-wt((alpha|beta) & 0x7fffffff).
Code: for each such addition and bit i < 31 the coordinates (alpha_i, beta_i, alpha_i ^ beta_i); a codeword's Hamming
weight is then exactly 2 x its trail cost.  Low-weight codewords are searched by information-set decoding (random
information sets, Lee-Brickell p <= 2).  A move must also change E1's inputs (Y1 Y6 Y12 m12 m5).
usage: python neutral.py <counter> <iterations> <seed>

inventory.name: oc stream
inventory.description:
oc_stream.c - streaming ones'-complement statistics of the front-line residual (2-round BLAKE3, pkgCG family).
Sampler = data/gen.c sample() (same constants, step CO, step CT, compression), but nothing is stored: every sample
updates the count layout defined in oclib.py layout() (quantities D, R, E, S; see oclib.py docstring).
  oc_stream real <out.bin> <N> <seed> <threads>   front-line pairs (fresh outer words, k, j each sample)
  oc_stream ctrl <out.bin> <N> <seed> <threads>   CONTROL: the 16 final-state words of A and of B uniform random
With threads=1 and seed 0x5045525350310001, mode real reproduces the rows of data/rand (same RNG order).
include <stdio.h>
include <stdint.h>
include <stdlib.h>
include <string.h>
include <omp.h>
define ROR(x, n) ((u32)(((x) >> (n)) | ((x) << (32 - (n)))))
define ROL(x, n) ROR((x), 32 - (n))
define MM 0xFFFFFFFFu

inventory.name: oclib
inventory.description:
Ones'-complement lens (Z/(2^32-1)) on the front-line residual: shared counting and evaluation.

Counts are built either in numpy (from the stored data) or by oc_stream.c (streaming, fresh samples); both
produce the SAME flat layout (layout() below), so one evaluator serves both.

Quantities, per residual word w in (1,3,4,6) (index 0..3):
  D  = oc(dA) - oc(dB) mod M          the residual read in ones'-complement coordinates (primary)
  R  = oc(dA ^ dB)                     the XOR residual R read as an element of Z/M
  E  = D - oc_diff(x) - oc_diff(y)     epsilon: what is left when D is split as E1 part + E3 part
                                       (digest word = x ^ y, x from one diagonal G, y from the other)
  S  = oc(dA) - oc(dA ^ R_other) mod M surrogate: D rebuilt with a residual from ANOTHER row (keeps R's
                                       distribution, breaks the dA <-> R coupling); a control, never tested
where oc(x) = x mod (2^32-1) (0xFFFFFFFF -> 0) and M = 2^32-1 = 3*5*17*257*65537.

inventory.name: offsets
inventory.description:
Rotation-offset census of the cyclic component of every k=1 design (counter 2, T1 free) in split_e3/designs.pkl.
For each loop word W (depends on the solved word g) compute O(W) = set of r in Z_32 such that bit i of W reads bit
(i - r) of g (rol by k adds k; XOR / modular add take the union; add also brings carries from lower bits).
Width of a set = shortest cyclic arc covering it (0 = single offset = T-function-like in a rotated frame).
Also counts, per design: loop length, additions with a g-dependent operand, XOR merges of two g-dependent
operands with different offsets, and whether T1 depends on g.
usage: python offsets.py  (writes offsets_out.txt)

inventory.name: orbits
inventory.description:
Torus maps of the 4x4 state and what they force on the message (shape_torus, 2026-10-08).

For a state map tau that preserves rows (G roles) and maps the column set and the diagonal set onto themselves,
a tau-symmetric 2-round trajectory needs, in each round, the message slot of a G call equal to the slot of its
image call.  The message words must then be constant on the orbits of the group generated by the round-0 slot
map and the round-1 slot map (pulled back through PERM).  #orbits = words of freedom left in the message.
Also lists which maps exist at all (row-preserving automorphisms of the column/diagonal structure).

inventory.name: origin test
inventory.description:
s3-2block-capacity / origin_test.py
Question: in a 2-block message, block-1 sets block-2's 512 capacity bits (chosen at cost ~2^c for c linear
conditions). Does a nonzero/chosen capacity enlarge the rounds-affine field for block 2, or deepen it
(2-round -> 3-round), relative to the single-block capacity=0 case?

Math being tested: affinity of a round map on a direction-span is governed by the SECOND finite difference
(cube sum over a pair of directions) = the polarization. For a degree-<=2 map this is a CONSTANT, independent
of the base point. The capacity is part of the base point. So capacity cannot change affinity of any map that
is degree<=2 on the field. W40 makes rounds 0-1 affine, so F2 is degree 2 and F3 = chi3 o affine is degree 2
on W40 -> origin-independent. This script verifies it on the organizer round function (cd.rnd, verified vs
keccak.py by cd.selfcheck).

Outputs per round depth k=1..4:
  - affine_defect_rank: GF(2) rank of the set of 2nd differences {D_wi D_wj F_k} over W40 pairs
    (0 => F_k is affine on all of W40; >0 => not affine, max affine subspace is smaller).
  - cap_variant_mismatches: number of pairs whose 2nd difference DIFFERS between capacity=0 and a
    random capacity base (and a second random base). 0 => capacity provably irrelevant at this depth.
Control: random SOURCE directions outside W40 (chi1 already quadratic) -> F3 2nd diff SHOULD depend on capacity.
Usage: python origin_test.py SEED NPAIRS

inventory.name: Pallas base field modulus.
inventory.description:
Organizer-owned byte-message Poseidon reference implementation.

The target is the Poseidon instance deployed in Zcash Orchard: `PoseidonHash`,
the `P128Pow5T3` parameter set over the Pallas base field. Width 3 with rate 2
and capacity 1, S-box x^5, R_F = 8 full rounds (four leading and four
trailing) and R_P = 56 partial rounds between them, so 64 rounds in total.
Each round adds its round constants to all three state elements, applies the
S-box (to every element in a full round, to element 0 only in a partial
round), then multiplies the state by the MDS matrix.

Reduced variants execute rounds 0 through rounds-1 of that fixed deployed
schedule and stop. This is a prefix reduction, so round i always uses row i of
the deployed round constants and the deployed MDS matrix is never regenerated.
Rounds 0 to 3 and 60 to 63 are full; rounds 4 to 59 are partial. Any prefix
from 1 to 64 rounds is supported; the hash mode, initial state, message
encoding and output encoding are always exactly as deployed.

Hashing uses the deployed `ConstantLength<2>` domain: a message is exactly two
field elements, the initial state is [m0, m1, 2^65] where the capacity element
is L * 2^64 with L = 2, one permutation is applied, and the output is state
element 0. No padding block is ever appended at this length.

A message is exactly 64 bytes: two 32-byte little-endian field elements, each
strictly less than p. Non-canonical encodings are rejected, because x and
x + p would otherwise encode one field

inventory.name: per basis vector, the operand patterns of every addition
inventory.description:
Period-k ('tandem repeat') difference subspace of 2-round BLAKE3, XOR-linearised (every + replaced by XOR).

A 32-bit word whose bit pattern repeats every k bits (k | 32) stays such a word under ANY rotation: ROR_r acts as a
rotation of the k-bit pattern by r mod k.  So the carry-free (XOR) model of the compression maps period-k message
differences to period-k state differences.  For k = 4: 4 GF(2) coordinates per word, 64 message coordinates,
output fold out[i] = v[i]^v[i+8] has 32 coordinates.  The kernel = carry-free colliding characteristics inside the
subspace.  This script builds the linear map, the kernel basis, and for each of the 96 additions the linear map to
its two operand patterns; it writes them for the C enumerator (p4enum.c) and prints the kernel dimension.
Usage: python period4.py [k=4]

inventory.name: pintest
inventory.description:
Own code (blake3-r3 dig, U55/U56 Q2).  Small-scale analogue of "pin one chain word": the chain state is ONE 32-bit word (digest word 0 fed into m8),
all other chain words m9..m15 are pinned constants (so the fed-back state is d = 32 bits), while the collision tag is n = 32 + e bits:
the 32 state bits plus the low e bits of digest word p (p = 4..7 for m12..m15: the word whose feedback is dropped).  A tag collision of two DIFFERENT
inputs is the goal (a restart is needed when the state itself repeats).  Random-function theory: every state collision (about sqrt(pi 2^32/2)
evaluations per trajectory) is a full-tag collision with probability 2^-e, so mean cost ~ 2^e * 1.25 * 2^16 against a 3-round BLAKE3 digest or an ideal function.
usage: pintest e runs rounds p mode(0 = BLAKE3 digest, 1 = ideal splitmix)

inventory.name: plan w
inventory.description:
Lemma 2 parameters (corrected conditional DP bounds) for a random function on N points, D distinguished points.
theta_lo = (D - SMAX) / N <= P(next fresh value is a DP | any history of at most SMAX values)
theta_hi = D / (N - SMAX) >= the same probability.
d = ceil(KD / theta_lo), gmax = ceil(H / theta_lo); S = n + d <= SMAX;
eps = e^-KD + n d / N + (S theta_hi + 1) e^-H + e^-TAB;  success >= 1 - exp(-n(n+1)/2N) - n/N - eps;
table overflow: Chernoff on Binomial(S, theta_hi) at mcap + 1 must be <= e^-TAB.

inventory.name: promo check
inventory.description:
Numerical sanity check of the promotion argument (NOTES section 4).

Promote = fix a word set P per sub-family; equations whose words all lie in P become setup constraints E_c.
Remaining system H' = (E - E_c) with P removed; its freedom F' = |words - P| - |E - E_c|.
Claim (DERIVED): H' has an empty 2-core only if E_c contains the whole 2-core of H, and then F' <= 0.
Test: random promotions built from random equation sets (grown along shared words), for every triple.
Usage: python promo_check.py <trials>

inventory.name: promote search
inventory.description:
Can PROMOTED family constants (a sub-family) plus per-call tables open the k = 3 sphere door?
Promote a set P of words to constants (chosen once, consistently, from one solution).  Equations whose words are
all constant drop out (paid once, at set-up).  Sub-family freedom F' = (vars - |P|) - (equations left); need
F' >= 3 words (2^96 >= 2^80 members).  0 per-member checks  <=>  generous table peeling (peel.py) empties the
system.  Search: greedy (add the word that shrinks the core most) + random sets biased to useful words.
Usage: python promote_search.py <held e.g. 0,2,5> <random_trials> <seed>

inventory.name: r0cost
inventory.description:
b3-misc/r0cost.py -- cell r0 x cost.

Using the front line's free words as listed in BLAKE3_2ROUND_MAP.md 2.5
(seven outer words C0.d1, D2.a1, D2.b1, S11, S4, X9, w6; member y = Y4;
trial word c1 = E1.c1; counter t_lo free and solved), propagate the word
relations of round 0 + round-1 columns + E1's first half, one assignment at
a time, and classify every relation by what it depends on:
  context  - outer words only (run once per context)
  member   - needs y but not c1 (run per outer step)
  trial    - needs c1 (run per trial / inside the joint solver)
Then count round-0 relations in each class. This bounds what any saving in the
round-0 inverse step can be worth, given the map's charged rows.

inventory.name: r0swap
inventory.description:
b3-misc/r0swap.py -- cell r0 x cost, lever test.

The front line's omega test (omega = Y3 + y + w8) needs 8 member-level lines,
3 of them round-0 inverse lines (D0.d1, D0.a1, w8), because w8 depends on the
member y.  Lever: re-choose the outer words so that w8 is itself an outer word;
then omega costs one add per member and no round-0 line runs before the filter.
Test: replace one or two of the seven outer words (map 2.5) by w8 (and any
other word), keep y = Y4 (member) and c1 = E1.c1 (trial), t_lo solved, and ask
whether the whole system still resolves one assignment at a time, and at what
member-level / trial-level line counts.

inventory.name: r0tri
inventory.description:
b3-misc/r0tri.py -- cell r0 x cost, exact version of the w8-outer lever test.

Does ANY choice of the 7 outer words make the system (round 0 + round-1
columns + E1 first half, t_lo free) solvable one assignment at a time with
w8 an outer word, y = Y4 the member and c1 = E1.c1 the trial word?
ILP: each relation determines exactly one of its words (a matching), each word
is determined at most once, levels forbid cycles (l_w >= l_u + 1 whenever the
relation determining w contains u). Free words = the 9 unmatched words.
Control: the front-line set (map 2.5) must come out feasible.

Work per bucket is in thread-seconds of the local r3 profile (8 threads); each bucket runs at min(T, cap) threads with efficiency eff.

inventory.name: rank counter
inventory.description:
GAPS section 2 row 1 (const x alg on the counter base), step 1: rank every scored pin by the COUNTER objective

    C_ctr(pin) = max over beta of part(beta) x 2^k(beta)      (units 2^-128 per trial)

(the counter solve prescribes one beta, so its 2^-k is not paid by trials), and score it with the CENSUS one formula
    time_log2 = log2(0.5) + 128 - log2(C / m) + log2(ops / 430) + 0.02 + penalty
with m = 2.0 (ours; 1.4 = the board's), ops = 6.5 (H8's counted counter machine; a GUESS for every other pin), and
penalty 0 (a length pair without forced bytes).

Read only (nothing written outside this folder; bytecode writing off):
  research\catalogue\census\pins.py          (imported: the pin list and its per-beta file names)
  research\paths\paths_lib.py                (imported: walks(), the valid betas of a D11, and rol())
  the per-beta files that pins.py names, plus the second per-beta file of H8, L6a and L16a
  for the pins WITHOUT a per-beta file, the screens named in research\paths\ATLAS.md Table 1b:
     research\night\main\lx_totals.txt        (300 lightest betas: every beta with mass, "beta k positive part")
     research\night\main\cand_exact_lx.txt    (the pin search's own beta and its exact part; k computed here)
     astra-jobs\~archvie\...\task1_pins\out\totals.txt   (L8c: server, 1,000 lightest betas, heaviest beta)
Writes: rank_counter_out.txt, rank_counter.csv (this folder).

inventory.description:
Recount of the exact class-rate parts quoted in pkg5, pair by pair, with the night's calculator (source
research/night/main/pair_calc.c). The pin, the class and the list of betas come from tools/pkg5_data.py (the
betas with a nonzero part in the night's .total file, and the betas counted outside that list).

The calculator is built here afresh from its source with ONE change, in what it writes with -o: for every
outcome it also writes the two factors in full instead of two-decimal logarithms,
    E1 = the number of triples (c1, b1, a2) with this beta for which E1 produces (tau, eps)  [P1 * 2^(96 - k)]

    random-subset branch ("sampled") and the number of outcomes for which the exact E1 count fell back to
    the product formula ("formula fallbacks"); both must be 0 for the word "exact";
  - a line OUTS per beta: of the outcomes with a nonzero E3 count ("positive" in the PAIR line), how many
    have a nonzero exact E1 count as well ("nonzero") and how many have an exact E1 count of zero ("zero");
  - a line OUTX per outcome with a nonzero product: tau, eps, E1 and N3 as integers.

inventory.name: ring gd
inventory.description:
Rings in the idea-1 system: cut-and-run-around orders, block-triangular structure, bit-level seed cost.

Word level (same model as ../gd_order.py): every G call = 8 primitive equations, each solvable for any one word.
A guess-and-determine order makes g guesses; F of them are the family index (F = freedom), the other g - F are
CUTS.  Each of the g - F checks is the closure of a ring through one or more cuts.  We match checks to cuts
(perfect matching, then strongly connected components = Dulmage-Mendelsohn blocks).  A block of size 1 is a
single-cut ring: cut one word, run around, close on one 32-bit equation.  A block of size b is a b-cut ring.

Bit level (bitgd.py): a block's subsystem (words that depend on its cuts and feed its checks) is solved by seeding
s bits and propagating; cost 2^s passes for ~1 root on average.  A block whose parameters (known, varying words
feeding it) number p can instead be tabulated once if 32*p + s <= 85 (memory free, preprocessing <= 2^85).

Sub-family: only 2^64 members are needed, so F - 2 index words may be frozen (they become constants for tables).
Usage: python ring_gd.py <fixed|outhalf> <runs> <seed> [maxguess] [bitTries]

inventory.name: rotscan
inventory.description:
rotscan.c - rotational lens on the front-line residual data (research/fifties/perspectives/data).

Scan AB : side-A word i vs side-B word j:  V = B_j ^ rotl(A_i, r)   (op x)
                                           V = B_j - rotl(A_i, r)   (op s, mod 2^32)
                                           V = ror(B_j, r) - A_i    (op r, i.e. B = rotl(A + c, r); S uses the XOR shuffle)
          for every i, j in 0..3, r in 0..31.  Lists: dig (digest words 1,3,4,6 A vs B),
          e1 (E1 outputs a2 b2 c2 d2, A vs B), e3 (E3 outputs e2 f2 g2 h2, A vs B),
          plant (digest A vs a synthetic B with planted rotational relations = positive control).
Scan WW : relations inside one 4-word set X:  V = X_j op rotl(X_i, r), (i,j,r) != (i,i,0).
          Sets: R (residual), K1, K3, DA (digest A), RP (R1, R3, U4 = R4^ROR(R1,8), U6 = R6^ROR(R3,8)).
Scan J  : joint over the four words, same r, word map identity:  sum_w HW(B_w ^ rotl(A_w, r)).

Sources (the control design):

inventory.name: sched
inventory.description:
Carry-graph (time-sweep) schedule for the cycle at word size n (rotations scaled by n/32; all cycle rotations are
multiples of 4, so n in {8,16,24,32} keeps the exact structure).  Each addition Z has a frame f_Z; at time t it
processes bit (t - f_Z) mod n.  Events (consumed by cg.c):
  G  w b      guess bit b of word w (g at first use; an addition output needed before it is computed)
  C  z m      guess the carry entering the first processed bit of z (m values), when that bit is not bit 0
  Z  z        carry of z := 0 (chain starts at bit 0)
  A  z j mode compute bit j of z (mode 0 store, 1 verify an earlier guess, 2 check = 0 for 'chk')
  V  z        verify the guessed carry of z (after bit f-1 of the wrapped chain)
plus the expected log2 live-branch level after each event (independent-bits model).
usage: python sched.py n [restarts] [seed] -> writes sched_n<n>.txt and prints the width profile

inventory.name: sep test
inventory.description:
Join lever check for the BLAKE3 2-round parent node (grid cell basextech / mode / join).

f(L, R) = compress(IV, L || R, t=0, len=64, flags=PARENT|ROOT=12, rounds=2), 256-bit digest.
L, R are the two child CVs (8 words each).  A list / k-list (Wagner) join on f needs output bits that split
as g(L) (+) h(R).  For such a bit the second-order derivative
    D = f(L,R) ^ f(L',R) ^ f(L,R') ^ f(L',R')                   (XOR form)
    A = f(L,R) - f(L',R) - f(L,R') + f(L',R')  mod 2^32          (modular-add form, per word)
is identically 0.  Parts (all against a compression cross-checked with hash-smash/verifier/blake3.py):
  T1 random      L, L', R, R' uniform; per-bit P(D=1) over N quadruples (all 256 bits)
  T2 add         same quadruples, per-bit P(A bit = 1) and P(A word == 0)
  T3 word-pairs  L, L' differ only in word i, R, R' only in word j (64 pairs): a join over 2^32 x 2^32
                 sub-lists would need separability on that subspace
  T4 bit-pairs   L' = L ^ (1<<k in word i), R' = R ^ (1<<l in word j), k,l in {0,7,15,31} (1024 pairs):
                 low-weight differences, where 2 rounds might not have mixed L into R yet
Flag rule: |P - 1/2| >= 2^-8 and z >= Bonferroni threshold; every flagged cell is re-measured on fresh
samples (16x) and counted only if it survives.  Usage: sep_test.py LOGN [seed] -> prints, writes sep.json

inventory.name: sepbound
inventory.description:
State-size bounds for exact bit-serial (carry-graph) solvers of the best cycle (21 equations), for two natural
processing orders.  For each modular addition that reads a loop word: number of loop-word operands and carry bits
per bit position (2 operands -> 1 bit, 3 or 4 operands -> 2 bits).  The check's offset set comes from offsets.py.
  position order (Sol D4 7.2 carry graph): a check bit at position i reads g at i - o for every offset o, so the
    state must hold the g bits of the covering arc (width w) plus one carry state per addition;
  slice order (positions mod 4, possible because every offset is a multiple of 4): the state must hold the
    carries that cross from in-nibble position 3 to position 0, at every nibble boundary of every addition.
usage: python sepbound.py  (writes sepbound_out.txt)

inventory.name: sequential counter (Sinz): sum(Os) <= bound

inventory.name: sha3 ldconn
inventory.description:
SHA3-256 r6, combo "low degree x connector": can the 2-round-affine field W40 carry a FIXED pair
difference through rounds 1-2 (and the chi3 conditions be paid in field dimensions), so that FES can enumerate
pairs of a differential trail cheaply?

For a coset t + W40 and a pair difference Delta (in the 320-bit source, embedded like W40: lanes 0-4 and 10-14,
lane 16 = 0x86<<56; or a general message-lane difference), the pair-difference function
    delta_r(w) = S_r(t + w) xor S_r(t + Delta + w),   w in W40
is affine in w for r <= 2 (both cosets are 2-round affine), and for r = 3 on the sub-field where delta_2 is
constant (derivative of a quadratic map).  Per stage we report:
  r=1,2: dim of the sub-field W'_r on which delta_r is constant (= 40 - rank of its linear part)
  r=2  : weight of delta_2 and its column-parity weight at theta3 (odd columns -> theta3 spread)
  r=3  : rank of delta_3's linear part on W'_2 (= linear chi3 conditions), dim W'_3
  r=4..6: sampled weight of delta_r on W'_3 (or W'_2) and the max per-bit bias.
Imports research/sha3r6/lowdegree/cube_degree.py (W40, organizer round function via SOLCLOUD_12 keccak).

inventory.name: shapegraph
inventory.description:
Exact shape facts (32-bit, no sampling).  Owner: shape_odd agent.
1. call-message graph: each message word links its round-0 call and its round-1 call -> cycle decomposition.
2. lattice symmetries: the 4x4 state is a torus Z4 x Z4 with rows = roles (a,b,c,d), columns and diagonals =
   G lines.  Find every map (r,c) -> (r, e*c + s*r + t) that sends columns to columns and diagonals to
   diagonals, its induced message-word map, whether it commutes with the message permutation, and whether
   it fixes the initial state.
3. Moebius / slide: the unique message M* whose round 0 returns the initial state (one round is a bijection,
   inverse formulas of ../../sol_answer_W_newpaths.md 3.3); then 2-round(M*) == 1-round(P M*).
4. Circle: per-word rotation-invariant sets and the birthday on rotation classes.

inventory.name: shapes
inventory.description:
Shape-family survey on toy 2-round BLAKE3 (numpy).  Owner: shape_odd agent.

families : does a geometrically shaped message family make any group of output words take FEWER values
           (collision rate above uniform)?  A family whose half-digest has collision entropy h bits gives a
           birthday cost of 2^((h + rest)/2); uniform means no gain.
           Ratio = observed colliding pairs / expected for uniform keys, among DISTINCT messages of the family.
twists   : pairs (M, tau M) for twists tau (rotation, message permutation P and powers, torus shift, transpose,
           mirror, palindrome, complement, negation, x<->y swap).  Measures: equality rate out_j(tau M) == out_i(M)
           (and == ROT(out_i(M)) for rotations), max bit correlation, max XOR/additive difference frequency,
           and the XOR-sum around the closed orbit (Moebius closure) for tau of finite order.
Usage: python shapes.py families <w> <log2N> [seed]  |  python shapes.py twists <w> <log2N> [seed]

inventory.name: sizecap
inventory.description:
sizecap.py: the method's size limit. What the counter lever is worth when the message length is capped.

A cap of L bytes means t <= (L - 63) / 1024, i.e. t < 2^k. Two ways to meet it (32-bit real arithmetic):
  F (filter): generate cube trials as the lever does and drop those with t >= 2^k;
  I (invert): per outer step, run every t < 2^k backwards through the bijection t -> c1 (about 14 word ops)
     and keep the c1 that fall in the T1 cube.
Part 1 (COMPUTED): over random outer steps, the mean number of cube members with t < 2^k (whole cube, 2^21 per
  outer step, for k = 12..32), and the same count by inversion for k = 12; spread across outer steps.
Part 2 (DERIVED, the one formula of counter\adjudicate\adj_check.py with ops GUESSES):
  time_log2 = 84.96 + log2(cost per kept trial / 6.5), against the filed 92.53.
  F: cost = 11 * 2^(32-k) + 6.5 (11 ops to reach t, GUESS); I: cost = (OUTER + 14 * 2^k) * 2^(11-k) + 6.5
  (OUTER = 400 ops per outer step, the census GUESS).
Part 3 (COMPUTED): speed of the organizer's Python _compress (2 rounds), to price a reference check of a pair.
usage: python -B sizecap.py NOUTER SEED

inventory.name: split

b3-misc/split.py -- cell const x join (GAPS item 5).

Question: can extra constants (one more pinned word, or any set of them) split
the front-line system so that E1's inputs and E3's inputs range independently
(a Cartesian product, so a list join on the 128-bit residual becomes possible)?

Method (word level, structural = generic counting, the guess-and-determine model):
  * Trace the reference 2-round compression (verifier/blake3.py) into word
    relations: each G call = 8 relations (a1=a+b+x, d1=ror(d^a1,16), c1=c+d1,
    b1=ror(b^c1,12), a2=a1+b1+y, d2=ror(d1^a2,8), c2=c1+d2, b2=ror(b1^c2,7)).
    Every relation is solvable for any one of its words given the others.
    The trace is checked against blake3._compress on random inputs.
  * System = round 0 (K0..K3, D0..D3) + round-1 columns (C0..C3).
    Fixed: init state, w4, w13, w14, w15, pins X3, X7, X11, X15; words forced by
    the fixed ones are propagated (so C3 is constant, as in the map).
  * Terminals: E1 inputs {Y1, Y6, Y12, w12, w5}; E3 inputs {Y4, Y9, Y14, w8}
    (Y3, Y11, w15 are constants).
  * A split labels every free word U (E1 side), V (E3 side) or S (constant /
    separator) and every relation U, V or S, with no relation touching both U
    and V. Structural dimensions: d_X = #words_X - #relations_X.
    d_U + d_V + d_S = dim (8 at the root, 9 with t_lo free, 10 with t free).
    The exact optimum over ALL labelings (so over every choice of extra
    constants) is found by an ILP (scipy milp / HiGHS).

inventory.name: stage cd
inventory.description:
Appendix E: stage C and stage D of one trial at r = 7, expanded into their totals (standard library only).
Run:  python3 stage_cd.py      prints S_C = 253,143,956,421,123 and S_D = 106,846,183,041,913 and asserts them.

The inputs are the dimensions m = (5^13 - 1)/2 = 610,351,562 (degree of the modulus), the exponent (p-1)/2, and the charging rules of section 4.2,
which fix the per-kernel charges in the tables PASS and K3 below (butterfly 3 field operations or 2 when the twiddle is 1, twiddle load with
address, 8 operations per radix-3 leaf, loop control 3 per iteration and 2 on exit). Everything else is a finite recurrence:
  stage C: transform sizes 3*2^a >= 2m-1 and >= m+1; Newton levels l -> min(2l, m-1); the exponent: 224 squaring steps, 45 of them with the multiplication by S;
           each step = one square convolution + two row-wise multiplication convolutions (conv_sq, conv_mulc_otf) + the linear loops;
  stage D: the outer loop of the Euclid driver, hgcd(k) with k halved (rounded up) until k <= 96, in each level the two recursive calls,
           apply_inv (one bilinear convolution), the division by a quotient of degree one, the 2x2 matrix product (conv_bilin_cost);
  below k <= 96 and n <= 192: classical division steps with quotient of two coefficients (divrem_naive).
`Tr` accumulates the operations and the number of live arrays (an allocation is charged 121 + 13 (2 live + 1), a free 105).

inventory.name: stage1
inventory.description:
Stage 1: every chi1 transition of every seed word; relaxed chi2; chi3-input K/N sets.
Seeds: the 1,749 linstruct3 cycle words (theta1 kernel, stopped chi1 output in theta2 kernel; 6 or 8 bits).
Per word v: A1 = P(v) (chi1 input, exact). chi1 output B1(tau) = base + sum tau_i g_i over the product of the row
affine spaces U(delta_row) = ALL compatible output differences (= every choice of neighbour constants).
A2(tau) = P(B1(tau)). chi2 relaxed (common.chi_relax_KN): K = chi3-input bits active for every chi2 choice,
N = bits never active. 'kp' = chi1 output in the theta2 CP kernel (no theta2 spread).
6-bit words: all 4^6 chi1 choices enumerated. 8-bit words: kp choices (solved exactly) + 4,096 random non-kp choices.
Writes stage1_kp.npz (all kp variants: word id, tau, A2, K, N) and stage1_stats.json.

inventory.name: struct split
inventory.description:
ctr x join, part S: structural (word-level) split search over EVERY triangular basis.

Uses the equation system of counter_next/knobs/model.py unchanged (imported).
A triangular basis = an orientation of the equations (each equation solves one of its words),
acyclic, every non-basis word solved exactly once.  With up to `max_checks` equations left
unsolved (checks), the basis grows by that many words.

Targets (from coupling.py diffs(), checked in RESULT.md):
  key1 (E1 side, 128 bits) is a function of T1 = {E1.a2, E1.b1, E1.d1}
  key3 (E3 side, 128 bits) is a function of T3 = {E3.h1, E3.g1, E3.f1, E3.e2}

Split (meet-in-the-middle) = a triangular basis B = U + V + Fx with
  T1 depending on no V word, T3 depending on no U word,
  T1 depending on some U word, T3 depending on some V word.
Then for each Fx, key1 = f(U) and key3 = g(V): a list join decouples the two sides.
With checks allowed, a check equation must contain no word that depends on both U and V
(so it is separable and can be joined on); gain needs min(|U|-cU, |V|-cV) > cX.

Dependency is structural (union over the solving equation's other words); a structural
non-dependency is an exact non-dependency.

inventory.name: t2 macros
inventory.description:
Generalised table rules with tables of up to 2^64 entries (preprocessing <= 2^64, allowed by the cost model).

For every G call and every subset Q of its 8 primitive equations: W = non-constant words of Q.
For every P subset of W with |P| <= 2: U = W - P.  Rule P -> U is valid when
  (1) |U| = |Q| and there is a perfect matching equations(Q) <-> U (each equation solved for a distinct word of it)
      [structural rank; a word pair that occurs only through one sum, like (a, x), fails here],
  (2) the solution set of Q (dimension delta = |W| - |Q| = |P|) can be enumerated by plain propagation inside Q
      from some delta words (so the table costs 2^(32 delta) <= 2^64 to build).
Per G call and P the targets of all valid Q are united; targets already reached by plain propagation from P
(inside the G call) are dropped.  Output: the system file of export_sys.py with these macros
(one line per target word).
Usage: python t2_macros.py <fixed|outhalf> <out>

inventory.name: t2 sibling
inventory.description:
TEST 1b + TEST 2 on toy 2-round BLAKE3 (xtoy.Toy).
Length-sibling pairs (fringe angle 3): base message M with block length b1, partner M' with length
b2 = b1 ^ 8 and m4, m5 adjusted so that K2's output - hence the whole round-0 state X - is identical.
The pair then differs only in m4 (round-1 C3 x input) and m5 (round-1 E1 y input).
Per instance (cv, counter, flags) we count:
  ZA   : dY7 = dY15 = 0  (E0/E2 inputs equal: the 'zero channel' of the A half; the filed path pins this)
  A    : out0,2,5,7 equal;      Afold = A and not ZA   (A half equal through XOR-fold cancellation)
  ZB   : E1 and E3 outputs equal (B 'zero channel');   B : out1,3,4,6 equal;  Bfold = B and not ZB
  full : all 8 output words equal (a real toy collision of the 2-round compression)
TEST 1b question: do these rates depend on the instance constants (chunk counter, flags, chaining value)?
TEST 2 question: how much of A and B comes through the XOR-fold channel (Rumba-style cancellation)?

tree_check.py  (scout_recent; research only)
Checks, with the ORGANIZER's reference (hash-smash\verifier\blake3.py, imported read-only, rounds=2), that the
digest of  P || X  (P = t full 1024-byte chunks, X = a 55- or 63-byte last chunk) depends on X only through the
chunk chaining value  CV_t(X) = first 8 words of compress(IV, X, counter=t, len(X), CHUNK_START|CHUNK_END).
So two last chunks with equal CV_t give a full 2-round BLAKE3 collision of P||X and P||X'.

inventory.name: tree check
inventory.description:
Part 1: the tree-mode claim on real messages, organizer verifier (2 rounds).
M = P||X, M' = P||X', P = t identical full chunks, X of 55 bytes, X' of 63 bytes.
Checks per t:
 (a) organizer digest(P||X) == own root_from_stack(own stack(P), own CV_t(X))  [digest is a function of CV_t(X)]
 (b) the organizer's own last-chunk descriptor is (IV, words(X), counter t, len, flags 3) and its
     _compress gives the same CV as the own code; the v12/v13 it feeds are t & mask, t >> 32
 (c) planted CV collision: patch the organizer _compress so that ONLY the last-chunk compression of X'
     returns the CV of X; the organizer then outputs equal digests for P||X and P||X'  (equal CV => equal digest)
 (d) unpatched digests of P||X and P||X' differ (different CVs give different digests here)
 (e) C program tree64 (own, SIMD + threads) equals the organizer digest (validation for the large-t run)
usage: python -B tree_check.py [nx]

inventory.name: twoblock
inventory.description:
S8 check: the filed 55/63 construction (pin H8) moved into the LAST block of a two-block message.

Block 0: 64 arbitrary bytes, flags CHUNK_START, CV = first 8 words of its 2-round compression (organizer reference).
Block 1: built like ../sidepaths/fam55.py but with v0..v7 = CV and flags = CHUNK_END|ROOT = 10.
The pin is kept in the CV-free coordinates T = X3 + X7 - K, Q = K + W4 (K = cv2 + cv6), X7, X11, X15, W13:
for a new CV, X3' = X3 + (K' - K_IV) and W4' = W4 - (K' - K_IV).

U08 m5: how E1's a2-tau condition depends on the shift delta5 = w5' - w5 (the cancelled K2 word).
Criterion (proof.md 9.7, re-derived here and brute-force validated at width 10):
  exists a with a ^ (a+Delta) = tau  iff  d=(tau-Delta) even, d/2 has no bit outside tau (tau[top]=0);

brute-force validation of the criterion at width 10 (tau[top]=0)

inventory.name: unif control: same scan shape on uniform words (one pass, xor and add only, all r) to get the null max
inventory.description:
Joint lens: rotation ("spiral") scan and windowed mutual information between the residual words.
Data: perspectives/data/rand/res.u32 (2^20 independent rows). Train = first half, test = second half.
Controls: SHUF = the partner word permuted within its half (keeps both marginals, kills the dependence);
          UNIF = uniform random 32-bit words of the same count (numpy PCG64, fixed seed).

Part A (spiral scan): for words i, j and r = 0..31, Z = R_i op ROR(R_j, r) with op in {xor, add, sub}.
  Collision entropy H2(Z) = -log2(collision pairs / C(n,2)) from n = 2^19 rows; uniform 32-bit gives about 32
  (32 expected pairs, sd about 5.7). Deficit = 32 - H2. z = (pairs - pairs_shuf) / sqrt(pairs_shuf + 1).
Part B (windowed MI): 8-bit cyclic windows at start p in R_i and q in R_j, all 6 pairs, all p, q (6144 windows).
  Plug-in MI in bits; the same statistic on SHUF gives the bias; excess = MI_data - MI_shuf.
  Offset profile: mean excess over p for each lag d = (q - p) mod 32.
Run: python spiral_mi.py > spiral_mi_out.txt

inventory.description:
w8sel.py (counter_next/knobs; research only): how much is choosing w8 per outer step worth?

v13 solved per outer step (a 2^-13 filter on outer steps) lets w8 be prescribed next to Y4 (knobs_model_out.txt).
w8 enters E3 only in e2 = e1 + f1 + w8 = c + f1 with c = e1 + w8, c' = c + DY3 (DY3 = Y3' - Y3).  First-order

inventory.name: walsh
inventory.description:
walsh.c - joint lens: every GF(2) mask of weight 1..4 over the 128 residual bits, with train/test and controls.
  walsh <res.u32> <raw|spiral> <rows> <seed> [maxw]
Coordinates: raw    W = (R1, R3, R4, R6)
             spiral W = (R1, R3, R4 ^ ROR(R1,8), R6 ^ ROR(R3,8) ^ ROR(eta,8))   (a linear bijection of R; RESULT.md s.2)
Data sets (each split into train = first rows/2, test = last rows/2; shuffles act within each half):
  D  = data;  S1, S2 = data with each of the 4 words permuted independently (keeps every word's own law,
  destroys cross-word dependence);  U = uniform random words (splitmix64, same count).
For mask a: c = E[(-1)^(a.W)].  Raw test: D against U.  Cross-word test: excess x = c_D - c_S1 against the
control excess c_S2 - c_S1 (exactly 0 for one-word masks).  z = c*sqrt(n), z_x = x*sqrt(n/2), n = rows/2.
Discovery on train at |z| > ZT, confirmation on test at |z| > 3 with the same sign.

include <string.h>
include <math.h>
include <omp.h>
define ROR(x, n) ((u32)(((x) >> (n)) | ((x) << (32 - (n)))))

inventory.name: word level
inventory.description:
Stage 2: pair / triangle search over the kernel-preserving (kp) transition variants of the 1,157 seed words.
A pair of directions (a, b) can sit in one 3-round affine field only if, on span{a,b}:
  chi1 input (exact, fixed per word), chi2 input (exact per variant), chi3 input (relaxed K/N per variant)
have no adjacent row positions whose forms are fixed, nonzero and different (common.conflict).
Each direction's real chi3-input difference is a single-direction trail, so it contains K and avoids N (sound).
Word level first (AND of K/N/A2 over a word's variants = weakest constraints), then variant level for survivors,
then triangles = three words with pairwise-compatible variants that agree (one variant per word).
Writes stage2.json.
